Prusa's INDX conversion manual and CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade manual, flattened into the single order prescribed by Prusa's companion article. Every step links back to its original. Colour bullets match the markers in the photos, as on help.prusa3d.com. Progress is saved in this browser only.

COMPANION ARTICLE

Companion article: introduction

source ↗

If you received your Prusa CORE One INDX conversion kit with the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade, or bought the Gen 2 upgrade separately and want to install both at the same time, this article will help you with the process. Read the instructions and information in this article thoroughly.

If you received the CORE One+ GEN 2 upgrade as part of your Prusa INDX conversion kit, note that all the GEN 2 upgrade parts (belts, Pulleys, spacers, fasteners, etc.) are included in the UPGRADE box.

There are some differences between the Prusa CORE One INDX and the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 guides. We will inform you when to switch to each guide with a handy link to the corresponding step.
In both guides, you will be alerted when you should switch back to this article.

How to navigate through the manual

  • Use the graphical navigation buttons in the bottom right corner or the arrow keys on your keyboard:
  • Play backward button / Up arrow key - Moves to the previous step.
  • Left arrow button / Left arrow key - Moves to the previous image, or to the previous step if it’s the first image in the step.
  • Next button / Right arrow key - Moves to the next image, or to the next step if it’s the last image in the step.
  • Play forward (Next) button / Down arrow key - Moves to the next step.
  • Click on Contents to expand the full list of steps in this guide. This allows you to jump to any step regardless of the sequence.
  • Click on Comments to open the discussion for a specific step and leave your feedback.

View high resolution images

  • When you browse the guide on help.prusa3d.com, you can view the original images in high resolution for clarity.
  • Just click on the image to open it in high resolution for a detailed view.

Before you begin

INDX 1.3 source ↗
  • NoteIf you plan on installing the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, follow the instructions here: Conversion of the PRUSA INDX Core One to Gen 2
  • ReminderThe INDX Conversion kit is compatible with the Prusa CORE One and CORE One+. This guide uses the CORE One+; some disassembly steps may vary between models.
  • The required steps depend on your printer’s current state:
  • If your CORE One+ is brand new and still unboxed, first follow the CORE One+ Unpacking & First run guide  before installing the INDX conversion.
  • If you already use the CORE One+ and purchased only the INDX Conversion kit (Founders Edition) you can continue with this guide.
  • CautionDo not discard any removed parts until instructed. Some parts will be reused later in the upgrade.
  • NoteThis guide is for both the 4-tool and the 8-tool PRUSA Core One/+ INDX conversion kit.
  • Some photos may show the 8-tool version. This does not affect the conversion process for the 4-tool version.

All the required tools are included

INDX 1.4 source ↗
  • Tools required for this upgrade:
  • ReminderUse the tools originally included with your CORE One+ / CORE One printer.
  • Needle-nose pliers (1x)
  • Philips (PH2) screwdriver (1x)
  • Universal wrench (1x)
  • Allen key set
  • Torx key set
  • NoteThe T10 screwdriver is included only with kit versions and may not be available with fully assembled printers. 
    It is not required, but may be more convenient in some steps.
  • We also recommend printing out the community-made Snap-rivet-remover

Labels guide

INDX 1.5 source ↗
  • All the boxes and bags including parts for the build are labeled.
  • The labels include the list of contents and part count.
  • You can download a Cheatsheet with 1:1 fastener drawings from our site prusa.io/C1-INDX-cheatsheet. Print it at 100 % on A4 paper, don't rescale it, otherwise, it won't work.
  • NoteFor PRUSA veterans: Fasteners are divided into individual bags according to its type. Not into packages for individual chapters, as it was with previous printers.
  • ReminderThe instructions will specify the package for each part, with the exception of fasteners, which are always located in the Fasteners package.

Spare bag

INDX 1.6 source ↗
  • Spare fasteners are included in each bag of fasteners. The amount of spare is always included in the total number shown on the bag.
  • Similarly, some parts may include one extra piece in the same bag.

Printed parts - versioning

INDX 1.7 source ↗
  • Most of the 3D printed parts are marked with their version.
  • E, F and Gx series (e.g. E1) - those parts are printed on Prusa Research farm and are distributed with the kit.
  • R, S and Tx series (e.g. R1) - those parts are available for download at https://www.printables.com/model/1758233-core-one-indx-printed-parts. They are identical to the factory ones.
  • The numbers indicate minor revisions that usually involve small design tweaks. A different label in the manual (e.g., a different version shown in photos) does not affect the assembly – all versions are fully compatible.
  • Noteif you have issues while assembling the printer with a specific printed part, find the label and share it with our support team.

We are here for you!

INDX 1.8 source ↗
  • Lost in the instructions, missing screw or cracked printed part? Let us know!
  • You can contact us using the following channels:
  • Using comments under each step.
  • Using our 24/7 live chat here at help.prusa3d.com
  • Writing an email to info@prusa3d.com

Pro tip: inserting the nuts

INDX 1.9 source ↗
  • 3D printed parts are very precise, however, there still might be a tolerance in the printed part and the same goes for the size of the nut.
  • Therefore it might happen, that the nut won't fit easily in or might be falling out. Let's see, how to fix it:
  • Nut won't fit in: use a screw with a thread along its entire length (typically: M3x10, M3x18) and screw it from the opposite side of the opening. While tightening the screw, the nut will be pulled in. Remove the screw afterwards.
  • Nut keeps falling out: Use a piece of tape to fix the nut temporarily in place, as soon as you insert the screw in, you can remove the tape. Using glue isn't recommended as it can partly reach into the thread and you won't be able to tighten the screw properly.
  • Every time we recommend using the "screw pulling technique", you will be reminded with Joe's avatar ;)
  • NoteParts in the pictures are used as an example.

Electronics protection (ESD)

INDX 1.10 source ↗
  • CautionWARNING: Make sure to protect the electronics against electrostatic discharge (ESD). Always unpack the electronics right before you need them!
  • Here are some tips to prevent damage to the electronics:
  • Keep the electronics inside the ESD bag right until you are asked to install them.
  • Always touch the sides of the board only while handling it. Avoid touching the components on the surface.
  • Before you touch the electronics use any conductive (metal) structure nearby to neutralize the possible static charge from your hands.
  • Be extra cautious in rooms with carpets, which are often a source of electrostatic energy.
  • Clothes made of wool or certain synthetic fabrics can easily gather static electricity too. It is safer to wear cotton clothing for the assembly.

Optional CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade

INDX 1.11 source ↗
  • NoteThe Prusa INDX Conversion Kit for CORE One+ includes parts for the optional CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade.
  • The Gen 2 upgrade is not required for the Prusa INDX upgrade.
  • If you want to install the Gen 2 parts, use the companion article below. It tells you when to switch between this guide and the CORE One+ Gen 2 Upgrade guide.
  • Conversion of the PRUSA INDX Core one to Gen 2
  • We recommend keeping the companion article open throughout the assembly.

Removing the MMU3

INDX 1.12 source ↗
  • ReminderIf your printer is equipped with the MMU3, it must be removed before continuing.
  • NoteThis step applies to both the MMU3 Lite (left) and the MMU3 Enclosed (right).
  • CautionTurn off the printer and disconnect it from the power.
  • To remove the MMU3, follow the MMU3 assembly guide in reverse order. The guide is available on the MMU3 product page prusa.io/mmu3.
  • Once the MMU3 has been removed, return to this guide and continue with the next step.

Reward yourself

INDX 1.13 source ↗
  • Converting your CORE One+ to the INDX CORE One+ is a rewarding experience. After finishing each chapter, reward yourself. There is a bag of Haribo bears in the box just for that!
  • Do not eat all the bears before you start or at once! Not following instructions will have serious consequences. We are currently assembling the Prusa Haribo tactical squad for this matter.
  • After years of scientific research, we came up with a solution.  Throughout the guide, we will tell you exactly how many bears to consume.
  • Eating an incorrect amount than prescribed in the manual might lead to a sudden boost of energy. Please consult a professional in the closest candy store.
  • CautionCut open the bag of the Prusa Haribo carefully so the gummy bears don’t spill onto the table. This step is very important!
  • CautionHide the Haribo for now! From our experience, an unattended bag with sweets might suddenly disappear. This phenomenon is confirmed by multiple cases all around the world.

Prepare your desk

INDX 1.14 source ↗

  • Clear your workspace. Make sure you have enough room. A nice clear flat workbench will get you the results you are aiming for.

  • Let there be light! Make sure you are in a well-lit environment. Another lamp or even an extra flashlight will probably come in handy.

  • Prepare something to contain the plastic bags and the removed packing materials so you can recycle them afterwards. Make sure there are no important parts being discarded.

  • A minimum working space of 1.5 × 1.5 meters (60 × 60 inches) is recommended.
  • CautionWe highly recommend placing a soft pad on your workbench. Some sheet metal parts have sharp edges that could scratch the surface.
  • NoteYou can use a piece of cardboard as a protective pad.
  • Let's start with chapter 2. Printer preparation & dissasembly.

INDX 2. Printer preparation & disassembly steps all of 36 · Easy

Tools necessary for this chapter

INDX 2.1 source ↗
  • For this chapter, please prepare:
  • 2.0mm Allen key
  • 2.5mm Allen key
  • T10 key / screwdriver
  • Needle-nose pliers or flush cutters for cutting zip ties
  • PH2 screwdriver
  • Universal wrench

Important: Update the firmware

INDX 2.2 source ↗
  • CautionComplete this step before disassembling the printer.
  • ReminderBefore you begin, make sure your printer is running firmware version 6.5.3 or newer.
  • On the printer display, go to Info -> Version Info -> Firmware Version to check your current version.
  • If your printer is already running firmware 6.5.3 or newer, continue to the next step.
  • CautionIf your firmware is older, update it before starting the upgrade.
  • Follow our dedicated firmware update guide for detailed instructions How to update firmware.
  • Once the firmware update is complete, return to this guide and continue.

Moving the Z-axis

INDX 2.3 source ↗
  • NoteBefore you begin, move the heatbed to an accessible position.
  • CautionDuring this step, keep the printer door closed and do not reach inside.
  • In the printer menu, go to Control -> Auto Home.
  • After Auto Home, move the heatbed down via Control -> Move Axis -> Move Z until the highlighted screws and the underside of the heatbed are accessible (minimum 200 mm).
  • NoteThis ensures both areas will be comfortably accessible during the procedure, as they will need to be handled later in the manual.

Unloading filament

INDX 2.4 source ↗
  • Make sure no filament is loaded in the printer.
  • Unload the filament. Visit the menu Filament and select Unload filament.
  • Unload the filament from the printer.
  • Remove the filament spool from the printer.

Powering off & protecting the printer

INDX 2.5 source ↗
  • CautionBefore you begin, make sure the printer has cooled down to ambient temperature.
  • Turn the printer off using the switch on the back.
  • Disconnect the printer from power.
  • Remove the steel sheet.
  • Place an empty cardboard box (e.g., a Prusament box) on the heatbed to protect it in case any parts fall.
  • Remove the USB drive to prevent damage while handling the printer.

Disconnect the Buddy3D camera

INDX 2.6 source ↗
  • If your printer is equipped with a Buddy3D camera, remove it before starting this procedure.
  • NoteThe Buddy3D camera is magnetically attached.
  • Disconnect the cable.
  • Remove the camera.
  • Place the camera in a safe location during the procedure. We recommend covering the lens with a protective cap that was included with the camera.

Do not discard removed parts

INDX 2.7 source ↗
  • CautionDo not discard any printer parts during this procedure.
  • Some of the removed printer parts will be reused later and are listed at the end of this chapter in the Parts recap steps.
  • Regarding the fasteners, we recommend keeping all removed screws.
  • NoteSome of the removed screws will be reused during the conversion. We recommend labeling these as you set them aside.

Removing the top nylon rivets

INDX 2.8 source ↗
  • There are four nylon rivets on the top panel that secure it. Remove these nylon rivets as follows:
  • Using needle-nose pliers, carefully grasp the rivet head with the tip of the pliers and pull it out.
  • NoteYou can also use the previously mentioned Core-one-snap-rivet-remover
  • CautionBe careful not to damage the top panel.
  • If the lower part of a rivet remains in the panel, grasp it with pliers and remove it as well.

Removing the top panel

INDX 2.9 source ↗
  • Remove the top panel from the printer.
  • NoteYou will not need the top panel for this upgrade.
     
     

Removing the top profile

INDX 2.10 source ↗
  • Using the 2.5mm Allen key, remove the two M3x4 screws from the top front panel.
  • From the front, use a T10 key to remove the two M3x4rT screws.
  • Carefully remove the top profile from the printer.

Removing the door

INDX 2.11 source ↗
  • NoteWe highly recommend that you remove the door. This will make moving and turning the printer a lot easier and safer during the INDX conversion.
  • Loosen and remove two M3x5rT screws securing the door panel in both hinges.
  • CautionIt is essential to hold the door panel securely while loosening the screws to prevent it from falling.
  • ReminderStart removing the screws from the lowest.
  • Carefully slide the door panel out of the hinges.
  • Place the door panel and the four screws in a clean and safe area to avoid any damage.
  • ReminderEnsure that the shaft that is inside the hinge does not fall out. If the shaft falls out, insert it back in, or set it aside along with the hinge part. We will mount these back on at the end of the assembly.

Accessing the electronics

INDX 2.12 source ↗
  • On the inside of the printer, remove the two M3x4rT screws holding the back cover.
  • On the back of the printer, slide the center cover downwards.
  • ReminderIf it’s difficult to move, use a screwdriver as a lever through the opening to assist.
  • Ensure the four hooks on top of the cover have disengaged from the metal chassis.
  • Remove the cover from the printer.

Accessing the buddy board

INDX 2.13 source ↗
  • Unscrew all six M3x4rT screws securing the electronics sheet (xBuddy box cover).
  • Slide the xBuddy box cover out of the electronics box and remove it from the printer.

Unplugging the cable I.

INDX 2.14 source ↗
  • Using a PH2 screwdriver, unscrew the two 6‑32 screws and disconnect the heatbed power cables from the xBuddy.
  • Pro tip: After disconnecting the cables, loosely thread both screws back in by at least three turns so they are not lost.
  • Disconnect the heatbed thermistor cable from the xBuddy board.
  • CautionThe cable connector has a safety latch. It is necessary to press the latch before disconnecting the cable.
  • Carefully cut the zip ties along the right side of the xBuddy box.
    Do not cut the lower cable tie.
  • CautionAvoid cutting any cables.
  • NoteCable ties can be cut using flush cutters, if available.

Unplugging the cables II.

INDX 2.15 source ↗
  • CautionThe cable connector has a safety latch. It is necessary to press the latch before disconnecting the cable.
  • Disconnect the Nextruder main cable from the xBuddy board.
  • Disconnect the side filament sensor from the xBuddy extension board.
  • Disconnect the RGB LED cable from the xBuddy extension board.

Removing the cables

INDX 2.16 source ↗
  • Route the disconnected cables out of the xBuddy box through the corresponding openings at the top.
  • CautionDo not pull on the cables if you feel any resistance.
  • NoteThe Nextruder main cable may pass through either the right or left opening, depending on when the printer was assembled.
  • Be careful not to remove the grommets - but don’t worry, they can be easily reinserted.
  • Cut the zip ties securing the cable harness.
  • CautionAvoid cutting the cables.

Pushing the cables in

INDX 2.17 source ↗
  • Slide the upper grommet slightly out of the opening to prevent it from falling into the printer while routing the cables.
  • Route the Nextruder main cable through the upper oval opening completely into the printer.
  • Reinsert the grommet into the oval opening.
  • Route the side filament sensor cable through the lower oval opening into the printer.
  • NoteSome of our printers do not have the grommet on the lower opening. This does not affect the process.

Guiding the heatbed cables in

INDX 2.18 source ↗
  • Cut and remove the zip tie securing the heatbed cable bundle.
  • Guide the heatbed cable bundle into the printer.
  • Leave all loosened cables freely inside the printer. You will return to them later.

Releasing the main cable

INDX 2.19 source ↗
  • Turn the printer so that its left side faces you (the side without the spool holder).
  • Release the five cable straps.
  • Focus on the area behind the Y-axis motor.
  • Using a 2.5 mm Allen key, loosen the M3 screw securing the cable clip.
  • No need to remove the screws from the part. Let the Nextruder main cable hang freely together with the cable clip.

Removing the LoveBoard cover

INDX 2.20 source ↗
  • Let’s move onto the left side of the Nextruder.
  • Using the 2.5mm Allen key, remove the M3x10 screw holding the side cover.
  • Remove the cover.
  • Unlock the Idler-swivel.
  • Open the idler assembly fully.

Disconnecting the Nextruder cables - left

INDX 2.21 source ↗
  • CautionEach connector has a safety latch. It is necessary to press the latch before disconnecting. Otherwise, the connector may get damaged.
  • Disconnect all cables on the left side of the LoveBoard.
  • Do not disconnect the Nextruder main cable connector.

Disconnecting the Nextruder cables - top

INDX 2.22 source ↗
  • CautionEach connector has a safety latch. It is necessary to press the latch before disconnecting. Otherwise, the connector may get damaged.
  • Disconnect the extruder motor cable.

Disconnecting the Nextruder cables - right

INDX 2.23 source ↗
  • Using the Allen key, remove two M3x6 screws securing the right cover on the Nextruder.
  • Remove the cover.
  • CautionEach connector has a safety latch. It is necessary to press the latch before disconnecting. Otherwise, the connector may get damaged.
  • Disconnect both cables from the right side of the LoveBoard.

Disconnecting the PTFE tube

INDX 2.24 source ↗
  • Slide the bowden-bend over the fitting in the Nextruder.
  • Press the black collet in the fitting down, preferably using two fingers.
  • Pull the PTFE tube out of the fitting.
  • Remove the bowden-bend from the PTFE tube.

Removing the Nextruder fitting

INDX 2.25 source ↗
  • Using the 8mm cutout on the Universal wrench, remove the M5-4 fitting.
  • Using the Allen key, remove two M3x18 screws securing the heatsink fan.
  • ReminderAfter being released, the heatsink fan will likely hang on the cable. Leave it as it is for now.

Removing the Nextruder

INDX 2.26 source ↗
  • Remove three M3x10 screws securing the Nextruder assembly to the X-axis.
  • CautionCAUTION: While loosening the last screw, hold the Nextruder to prevent it from falling and damaging the printer.
  • Remove the Nextruder assembly from the printer.
  • Unhook the heatsink fan cable from the cable hook and remove the fan from the printer.

Removing the print fan

INDX 2.27 source ↗
  • Focus on the rear X-axis assembly.
  • On the back of the print head, remove the M3x25 screw holding the print fan.
  • Remove the print fan by lifting it up.
  • ReminderSet the print fan aside. It will be needed later for the new toolhead.
  • Remove the two M3x10 screws holding the cover on the back of the print head.
  • Remove the cover.
  • Dislodge the extruder main cable from the dedicated groove.

Removing the LoveBoard

INDX 2.28 source ↗
  • Release and remove the M3x8rT screw securing the LoveBoard.
  • Remove the LoveBoard with the Nextruder main cable completely from the printer.
  • Loosen two M3x10 screws in the Loveboard-holder.
  • Remove the Loveboard-holder from the printer.

Removing the fan shroud

INDX 2.29 source ↗
  • Release and remove two M3x10 screws securing the Fan-shroud to the Nextruder holder.
  • Remove the Fan-shroud from the printer.
  • Using the T10 key, remove two M3x4rT screws mounting the Cable-clip.
  • Remove the Cable-clip from the printer.

Removing the side handle

INDX 2.30 source ↗
  • Take a close look at the input PTFE tube in the handle on the right side panel.
  • Push in the collet in the handle.
  • Pull out the PTFE tube.
  • Using the T10 screwdriver release two M3x8rT screws securing the handle and the filament sensor.
  • Remove the handle from the printer.

Removing the side filament sensor

INDX 2.31 source ↗
  • Shift your focus back inside the printer.
  • Carefully cut and remove the zip tie near the PTFE tube.
  • This releases the side filament sensor cable from the underside of the CoreXY frame.
  • Grasp the released side filament sensor on the inner side of the right side panel and remove it from the printer.

Removing the spoolholder

INDX 2.32 source ↗
  • Using the T10 screwdriver, remove the four M3x8rT screws inside the printer securing the spoolholder.
  • CautionBe careful not to scratch the heatbed.
  • While loosening the last screw, hold the spool holder in your hand and remove it from the printer.
  • CautionPlace the protective cardboard box back onto the heatbed.

Parts recap I.

INDX 2.33 source ↗
  • CautionKeep the following parts for the next steps.
  • NoteAny parts not listed can be set aside.
  • Sheet metal back cover (1x)
  • xBuddy box cover (1x)
  • Print fan (1x)
  • Print sheet (1x)
  • Cable tie (2x)
  • From the fasteners, we recommend keeping all removed screws.

Parts recap II.

INDX 2.34 source ↗
  • Door panel assembly (1x)

Haribo time!

INDX 2.35 source ↗
  • CautionCheck the number in the circle carefully. It shows exactly how many gummy bears to eat in this step. Do not eat more.
  • Eat six gummy bears.

Final step

INDX 2.36 source ↗
  • The printer is now ready for the INDX upgrade.
  • Proceed to the next chapter: 3. Z-axis upgrade.

INDX 3. Z-axis upgrade steps 1–10 of 39 · Moderate

Tools necessary for this chapter

INDX 3.1 source ↗
  • For this chapter, please prepare:
  • 2.5 mm Allen key
  • T10 key / screwdriver
  • Needle-nose pliers or flush cutters for cutting zip ties

Optional: Installing the Buddy3D Camera USB-C cable

INDX 3.2 source ↗
  • NoteThis step applies only if you purchased the Buddy3D Camera and plan to install it.
  • Now is the right time to install the USB-C cable included with the Buddy3D Camera.
  • To install the cable, follow the dedicated Buddy3D Camera for CORE One Installation guide.
  • ReminderDo not connect or mount the camera itself at this stage. This will be done at the end of the assembly.

Removing the heatbed cable cover

INDX 3.3 source ↗
  • Temporarily remove the protective cardboard box from the heatbed.
  • Focus on the heatbed cable area at the rear left.
  • Unscrew two M3x10 screws securing the CORE-One-bed-cable-cover-top.
  • Remove the CORE-One-bed-cable-cover-top.
  • NoteYou will no longer need the CORE-One-bed-cable-cover-top. We recommend removing it to avoid confusion with the new part.

Releasing the heatbed

INDX 3.4 source ↗
  • Pull the heatbed cable bundle out from underneath the heatbed.
  • CautionBe careful not to snag the cables. If you feel resistance, stop pulling immediately.
  • Remove the textile sleeve from the entire length of the cable bundle.
  • NoteSet the sleeve aside, you will need this part again later.
  • Ensure that the LED cable is removed from the CORE-One-bed-cable-cover-bottom before proceeding.
  • Release and remove eight M3x4bT screws securing the heatbed.
  • Release and remove the M3x12bT screw in the middle.

Removing the heatbed

INDX 3.5 source ↗
  • Carefully remove the heatbed out of the printer.
  • Remove it together with the cables leading from the heatbed.
  • Set the heatbed aside in a safe place, it will be needed again later.
  • CautionAfter removing the heatbed, a spacer remains loose on the Z-carriage. Keep it in a safe place for later use.

Heatbed spacers: parts preparation

INDX 3.6 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-C1-bed-spacer-rear (1x) found in the Heatbed bag located in the INDX 4/8T box
  • INDX-C1-bed-spacer-front (2x) found in the Heatbed bag located in the INDX 4/8T box
  • M3nN nut (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3x18 screw (4x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag

Inserting the spacer - left

INDX 3.7 source ↗
  • Focus on the front left Z-axis.
  • Remove the two M3x10 screws securing the Z-carriage to the Z-axis.
  • CautionDo not remove the screws from the trapezoidal nut.
  • Gently lift the Z-carriage so that a gap of approximately 8 mm (0.3 inches) is created between it and the bed mount.
  • Insert the Bed-spacer-front into the gap.
  • Position the part so it fits around the bed mount, then align the holes.

Securing the bed spacer - left

INDX 3.8 source ↗
  • NoteMake sure the two M3nN nuts inserted from below do not fall out of the bed mount.
  • Secure the spacer with two M3x18 screws.
  • Tighten the inner screw first.
  • Then tighten the outer screw.

Inserting the spacer - right

INDX 3.9 source ↗
  • Focus on the front right Z-axis.
  • Remove the two M3x10 screws securing the Z-carriage to the Z-axis.
  • CautionDo not remove the screws from the trapezoidal nut.
  • Gently lift the Z-carriage so that a gap of approximately 8 mm (0.3 inches) is created between it and the bed mount.
  • Insert the Bed-spacer-front into the gap.
  • Position the part so it fits around the bed mount, then align the holes.

Securing the bed spacer - right

INDX 3.10 source ↗
  • NoteNote that there are two M3nN nuts inserted into the bed mount from below. Ensure that these do not fall out.
  • Secure the spacer with two M3x18 screws.
  • Tighten the inner screw first.
  • Then tighten the outer screw.
  • ReminderIf you plan on installing the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, follow the instructions in this article: Assemblling the Prusa INDX Core One with the Gen 2 upgrade.
COMPANION ARTICLE

Securing the bed spacer - right, additional information

source ↗

Follow the Prusa INDX guide from the start.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE BED SPACER - RIGHT, then read the instructions below in this article:

Before you move on to the next step in the Prusa INDX guide, we need to disconnect the X and Y motor cables and remove the left side panel and cover from the printer to accommodate the GEN 2 upgrades.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Press the safety latch to disconnect the X and Y motor cables from the xBuddy board on the back of the printer.
  • Gently pull the X and Y motor cables slightly to create some slack while keeping the connectors inside the electronics compartment.

  • Remove all five nylon rivets securing the left top see-through side cover. Support the cover by hand when removing the last rivets to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the side cover from the printer and set it aside in a safe, clean place.
  • Remove the eleven nylon rivets securing the left side metal panel. Support the panel by hand when removing the last rivets to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the metal panel from the printer.

Once the motors are unplugged and the left panel and cover are removed, return to the Prusa INDX guide step REMOVING THE REAR BED SPACER, and continue from there.

  • You will notice that the left panel and side cover are still in place in the Prusa INDX conversion guide. Proceed as if the left side cover and panel were removed in the Prusa INDX guide.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE OFFSET SENSOR CABLE.

INDX 3. Z-axis upgrade steps 11–19 of 39 · Moderate

Removing the rear bed spacer

INDX 3.11 source ↗
  • Loosen two M3x18 screw securing the trapezoidal nut and the CORE-One-bed-spacer-rear (on the underside).
  • While loosening the screws, hold the CORE-One-bed-spacer-rear in place and remove it once they are loose.
  • ReminderLeave the screws in the trapezoidal nut.
  • NoteDiscard the CORE-One-bed-spacer-rear to avoid confusion with the new part. You will no longer need this part.

Assembling the INDX-bed-spacer-rear

INDX 3.12 source ↗
  • Insert two M3nN nuts into the Bed-spacer-rear and push them in as far as possible.
  • Insert the nuts with the nylon insert (blue plastic ring) facing up.
  • NotePro tip: Use the screw-pulling technique.

Mounting the INDX-bed-spacer-rear

INDX 3.13 source ↗
  • Focus on the rear underside of the heatbed, where you removed the original Bed-spacer-rear.
  • Hold the Bed-spacer-rear in the same orientation as shown and fit it around the rear Z-axis threaded rod.
  • Align the holes in the bed spacer with the M3x18 screws that you kept in the trapezoidal nut.
  • Secure the part by tightening the two M3x18 screws.

Offset sensor: parts preparation

INDX 3.14 source ↗
  • For following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-C1-offset-sensor-holder (1x) found in the Heatbed bag
  • INDX offset sensor (1x) found in the Filament Sensors box
  • M3x8rT screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • M3x10 screw (1x) you removed earlier
  • Offset sensor cable (1x) found in the Cables bag
  • Zip tie (4x)

Mounting the INDX offset sensor

INDX 3.15 source ↗
  • NoteThe printed parts shown may differ slightly from the parts included in your package.
  • Mount the offset sensor onto the Offset-sensor-holder.
  • Align the screw holes with each other.
  • CautionMake sure the PRUSA logo is facing up.
  • Ensure that the offset sensor is correctly positioned.
  • Secure the offset sensor in place with the M3x8rT screw.

    Do not overtighten the screw to avoid damaging the electronics.
  • Lead the offset sensor cable between the Z-carriage and the right side panel of the printer.
  • Take the end of the cable without a label.

Connecting the offset sensor cable

INDX 3.16 source ↗
  • Plug the offset sensor cable into the offset sensor board connector.
  • On the underside of the Offset-sensor-holder, locate the pocket shaped for the Z-carriage.
  • Place the Offset-sensor-holder onto the Z-carriage so the shapes fit together and the screw holes align.
  • Check the correct alignment. It must match the photo.

Securing the offset sensor assembly

INDX 3.17 source ↗
Companion article: insert the M3x10 screw but tighten it only a few turns. It is fully tightened after the Gen 2 expansion joints are aligned.
  • Secure the offset sensor assembly to the Z-carriage from the underside using the M3x10 screw. The screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Do not overtighten.
  • NoteIf you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade along with the INDX conversion, insert the M3x10 screw and tighten it with only a few turns.
  • We will let you know later on when to properly secure the offset sensor assembly to the printer.
  • Loop a zip tie around the screw in the LED panel assembly and secure it, but do not tighten it yet.
  • Lead the offset sensor cable through the zip tie. Tighten the zip tie and cut off the excess.

Guiding the offset sensor cable

INDX 3.18 source ↗
  • On the left side of the Z-carriage, use side cutters to remove the three highlighted zip ties.
  • NoteCutting the cable ties will release the RGB LED cable, which is secured by them.
  • Thread three cable ties through the Z-carriage and connect their heads on the underside. Do not tighten them yet.
  • Guide the offset sensor cable through the three zip ties.
  • Guide the RGB LED cable through the three zip ties.

Securing the offset sensor cable

INDX 3.19 source ↗
  • Tuck the offset sensor cable in between the Z-carriage and the LED panel.
  • Tighten all three cable ties and cut off the excess ends.
  • The cables before the first cable tie must not be sharply bent; leave a slight slack.
  • Make sure the cables are properly tensioned and not sagging along their entire length.
  • Route the offset sensor and RGB LED cables upward through the rectangular cutout in the Z-carriage.
  • ReminderIf you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, Assemblling the Prusa INDX Core One with the Gen 2 upgrade.

Removing old expansion joints

source ↗

Switch to the GEN 2 guide, step REMOVING OLD EXPANSION JOINTS, and continue from there.

  • You may note that the headbed in the GEN 2 guide is leaning on the back of the printer. Follow the instructions as if the heatbed assembly was removed; it does not affect the heatbed expansion joints installation.

Keep following the instructions in the GEN 2 guide until you finish step INSERTING THE HEATBED SPACER.

GEN 2 4. Heatbed upgrade steps 4–8 of 42 · Moderate

Removing old expansion joints

GEN 2 4.4 source ↗
  • Using a 2.0 mm Allen key, slightly loosen the M3x4r screw securing the expansion joint on the Z-carriage.
  • Slide the expansion joint off the screw.
  • NoteKeep the expansion joints. One of them will be reused for the nozzle wiper assembly.
  • Remove the M3x4r screw.
  • Proceed the same for the rest of the expansion joints.

New expansion joints: parts preparation

GEN 2 4.5 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • New expansion joint (8x)
  • Expansion joint screw (8x)
  • PTFE washer M3 (16x)
  • Heatbed spacer 10 mm (1x)
  • ReminderDo not confuse the new heatbed spacer with the old one. They look similar, but the new spacer is longer.

Installing the expansion joint screws

GEN 2 4.6 source ↗
  • Place the two PTFE washers on top of each other in the front threaded hole of the Z-carriage.
  • Insert the expansion joint screw through the washers into the threaded hole.
  • Tighten the screw fully, but do not overtighten.
  • NoteA small gap between the washers and the screw head is normal due to the screw's non-threaded section.
  • Proceed the same for the rest of the threaded holes.

Installing the new expansion joints

GEN 2 4.7 source ↗
  • Slide the new expansion joint with the groove on the underside onto the screw between the PTFE washers.
  • Orient the expansion joint with the groove facing away from the Z-carriage.
  • Repeat this process for all remaining expansion joints.
  • NoteThe final position will be adjusted in the following steps.

Inserting the heatbed spacer

GEN 2 4.8 source ↗
  • Double-check that all expansion joints are oriented correctly and that the grooves are facing outward.
  • Place the new 10 mm heatbed spacer on the threaded hole in the center of the Z-carriage.
  • ReminderIf you are assembling the Prusa INDX along with the GEN 2 upgrade, return to the article: Assembling the Prusa INDX Core One with the Gen 2 upgrade.

Removing the Bed-cable-cover-bottom

source ↗

Return to the Prusa INDX guide, step REMOVING THE BED-CABLE-COVER-BOTTOM, and continue from there.

  • The old expansion joints are visible in a photo in the Prusa INDX guide. Proceed as if the expansion joints were replaced.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide all the way until you finish step RELEASING THE BELTS, then read the instructions below in this article:

INDX 3. Z-axis upgrade steps 20–39 of 39 · Moderate

Removing the Bed-cable-cover-bottom

INDX 3.20 source ↗
  • Prepare the heatbed assembly.
  • Using the Torx key, remove the M3x10rT screw that keeps the Bed-cable-cover-bottom attached.
  • Remove the Bed-cable-cover-bottom.

Heatbed cable covers: parts preparation

INDX 3.21 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-C1-bed-cable-cover-bottom (1x) found in the Heatbed bag
  • INDX-C1-bed-cable-cover-top (1x) found in the Heatbed bag
  • Heatbed spacer 6x3.1x8 mm (1x) removed earlier
  • M3nN nut (3x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3x10rT (1x) removed earlier
  • M3x10 screw (2x) removed earlier
  • Textile sleeve 520 x 8 mm (1x) removed earlier

Assembling the Bed-cable-cover-bottom

INDX 3.22 source ↗
  • Insert the M3nN nut into the bottom hole in the Bed-cable-cover-bottom.
  • Route the heatbed thermistor cable outside the cover.
  • Insert the Bed-cable-cover-bottom under the heatbed power cables and slide the cover beneath the heatbed.
  • NoteThe M3nN nut may fall out during installation. You can hold it in place from the bottom with your finger.
  • Secure the Bed-cable-cover-bottom in place with the previously removed M3x10rT screw.

Securing the heatbed: parts preparation

INDX 3.23 source ↗
  • M3x12bT screw (1x) removed earlier
  • M3x4bT screw (8x) removed earlier
  • Zip tie (1x)
  • NoteIf you are installing the Gen 2 upgrade during the INDX conversion, you will need the new M3x14bT screw (1x) found in the Gen 2 upgrade kit.

Inserting the heatbed

INDX 3.24 source ↗
  • Place the heatbed spacer directly over the threaded hole in the center of the Z-carriage.
  • Carefully insert the heatbed assembly back into the printer.
  • Ensure that the spacer in the middle stays in place.
  • Secure the heatbed in place with the M3x12bT screw that you set aside when initially removing the heatbed. Do not fully tighten the screw yet.
  • NoteIf you are installing the CORE One Gen 2 upgrade, then use the M3x14bT screw as mentioned in the previous step.

Securing the heatbed

INDX 3.25 source ↗
Companion article: tighten the heatbed screws two turns only. Final tightening happens in the Gen 2 'Fixing the heatbed' step later on this page.
  • Insert the eight M3x4bT screws into the remaining holes in the heatbed. Do not fully tighten the screws yet.
  • NoteIf you are installing the Gen 2 update along with the INDX conversion, tighten the M3x4bT screws by two turns only! We will fully tighten them later. Skip to the next step now.
  • CautionIMPORTANT: The heatbed must be tightened in a specific order. Repeat the sequence multiple times, ensuring the final tightening after at least two rounds.
  • After all screws are in place, tighten them in the following sequence:
  • Center screw
  • First four screws (edges)
  • Last four screws (corners)
  • ReminderTighten the screws gently, but firmly.

Wrapping the heatbed cables

INDX 3.26 source ↗
  • Wrap the textile sleeve around the heatbed, RGB LED, and offset sensor cables.
  • Route the RGB LED and offset sensor cables into the Heatbed-cable-cover-bottom through the side channel.
  • Slide the textile sleeve at least 1 cm (0.39 in) into the cable channel.
  • Place the M3nN nut on your finger with the nylon insert (blue plastic ring) facing down.
  • From below, align it with the screw holes shown in the picture.
  • Then press the nut into the Bed-cable-cover-bottom from underneath until it is fully seated.

Covering the heatbed cables

INDX 3.27 source ↗
  • CautionBefore closing the cover, make sure no wires are sticking out to prevent them from being pinched by the top cover.
  • Place the Bed-cable-cover-top over the heatbed cables and align it.
  • Secure the Bed-cable-cover-top in place with the M3x10 screw.
  • While tightening, hold the M3nN nuts in the lower part to prevent them from falling out.

Guiding the heatbed cable bundle I.

INDX 3.28 source ↗
  • Lead the heatbed cables under the heatbed and behind the Z-axis threaded rod.

Guiding the heatbed cable bundle II.

INDX 3.29 source ↗
  • Route the cables through the rear panel one by one in the following order:
  • 1. Offset sensor cable
  • 2. LED RGB cable
  • 3. Heatbed thermistor cable
  • Finally, route the heatbed power cables (black and red).
  • Push the heatbed cables and the textile sleeve through the grommet hole.
  • No more than 1 cm (0.39 in) of the textile sleeve should protrude from the back side.

Securing the textile sleeve

INDX 3.30 source ↗
  • Guide the zip tie through the two holes under the heatbed cables and make a loop around the heatbed cable bundle (textile sleeve) on the inside.
  • Tighten the zip tie firmly and cut off the excess.

Removing the Bed-stop-rear

INDX 3.31 source ↗
  • Use a Torx key to remove the M3x8rT screw on the rear side of the printer.
  • Remove the three M3x8rT screws.
  • Remove the Bed-stop-rear.

INDX-C1-Bed-stop-rear: parts preparation

INDX 3.32 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-C1-bed-stop-rear (1x) found in the Heatbed bag
  • M3x8rT screw (4x) removed earlier
  • M3nS nut (3x) found in the fasteners 2/2 bag

Assembling the Bed-stop-rear

INDX 3.33 source ↗
  • The new Bed-stop-rear is labeled with an X.
  • Insert the M3nS nut into the Bed-stop-rear and push it fully down.
  • Always check through the screw hole that the nut is properly aligned.
  • From the same side, insert the second M3nS nut all the way into the part.
  • From the opposite side, insert the third M3nS nut into the part.

Installing the new Bed-stop-rear

INDX 3.34 source ↗
  • Place the Bed-stop-rear onto the rear Z motor threaded rod and rest it against the edge of the rear panel.
  • Mount the Bed-stop-rear onto the Z-Axis threaded rod and secure it in place with three M3x8rT screws.
  • NoteThe middle screw threads into the plastic, not into a nut. Expect slight resistance while tightening.

Securing the Bed-stop-rear

INDX 3.35 source ↗
  • Move to the back of the printer.
  • Locate the oval screw hole under the cooling fans.
  • The oval hole must be flush with the hole in the Bed-stop part on the opposite side.
  • To compensate, slightly raise the rear of the CoreXY assembly - just a few millimeters.
  • After aligning the holes, secure them with the M3x8rT screw.

Connecting the RGB LED + offset sensor cables

INDX 3.36 source ↗
  • Route the RGB LED cable and the offset sensor cable through the upper right opening in the xBuddy box.
  • Plug the RGB LED connector into the rightmost RGBW LED slot on the xBuddy Extension board.
  • Plug the offset sensor cable into the upper right PUB CAN slot on the xBuddy Extension board.

Connecting the heatbed cables

INDX 3.37 source ↗
  • Route the heatbed power cables and the heatbed thermistor cable through the left opening at the top of the xBuddy box.
  • Using the 6-32 terminal screw connect the black power cable to the left terminal slot on the xBuddy board. Tighten firmly.
  • Using the 6-32 terminal screw to connect the red power cable to the right terminal slot. Tighten firmly.
  • Plug the heatbed thermistor connector to the slot next to the power terminals.

Haribo time

INDX 3.38 source ↗
  • ReminderNow is the time for a well-deserved boost.
  • Eat six gummy bears.

Done

INDX 3.39 source ↗
  • Congratulations! You have just upgraded the Z-axis.
  • Let's go to the next chapter.

INDX 4. INDX Toolhead & Side filament sensors steps 1–3 of 71 · Moderate

Tools necessary for this chapter

INDX 4.1 source ↗
  • For this chapter, please prepare:
  • 2.0mm Allen key
  • 2.5mm Allen key
  • T10 key / screwdriver
  • Needle-nose pliers or flush cutters for cutting zip ties
  • PH2 screwdriver
  • Universal wrench

Loosening the belts

INDX 4.2 source ↗
  • NoteIn these steps, we will loosen the belts to make installing the Head-mounting-plate easier. We also need to lubricate the belt tensioner screw to prevent any issues in the future.
  • Place the protective cardboard/box back onto the heatbed.
  • The belt tensioning screws are located in the front profile under the upper hinge on both sides of the printer.
  • Using a 2.5 mm Allen key, loosen the left tensioning mechanism until the M3x30 tensioning screw no longer holds the idler. Remove the screw.
  • CautionEnsure the M3nS nut in the Belt-tensioner-pulley does not fall out!
  • Repeat the process on the right side of the printer.
  • ReminderKeep the tensioning screws at hand; we will need them later.

Releasing the belts

INDX 4.3 source ↗
  • Using the 2.5mm Allen key, remove four M3x10 screws securing the Nextruder holder.
  • Disengage all four belt ends from the Nextruder holder slots.
  • Remove the Nextruder holder.
  • NoteThis part will no longer be needed.
  • Let the loosened belts hang freely.
  • CautionCAUTION: Do not pull on the belts, as they could slip out of the motor pulleys and require full disassembly for reinstallation.
  • ReminderIf you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, return to the Prusa INDX GEN 2 article now.
COMPANION ARTICLE

Additional information and removing the belts

source ↗

Before you move on to the next step, we need to remove the right side panel and side cover from the printer to implement the GEN 2 upgrades.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Remove all five nylon rivets securing the right top see-through side cover. Support the cover by hand when removing the last rivet to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the side cover from the printer and set it aside in a safe, clean place.
  • Remove the eleven nylon rivets securing the right steel side panel. Support the panel by hand when removing the last rivet to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the metal panel from the printer.

With the right side panel and cover removed, read the information and instructions below in this article before proceeding:

In the following section, note the differences in photos and assembly process between the Prusa INDX conversion guide and the Gen 2 upgrade guide. These are listed below and do not affect the assembly process:

The PTFE tube leading to the filament sensor is removed in the Prusa INDX guide, but is visible in the GEN 2. guide.

The Bowden-guide is visible in the photos. It is also attached back onto the motor assembly in the GEN 2 guide. We will not need it for the Prusa CORE One INDX conversion process; you can remove it from the printer once it is detached from the motor mount.

Belt-tensioner screws:

During the upcoming belt exchange instructions in the GEN 2 guide, we recommend using the Prusa lubricant found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag in the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX conversion kit.

  • Apply a small amount of Prusa lubricant to the tip of both left and right M3x30 belt tensioning screws you removed earlier.
  • Spread the lubricant evenly around the entire thread and insert the screws back into the belt tensioner.
  • Skip this step when it later appears in the INDX guide.

With the above-mentioned information in mind, let's proceed with the Prusa CORE One+ GEN 2 upgrade and the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX conversion:

Switch to the GEN 2 guide step REMOVING THE BELTS, and continue from there.

Keep following the instructions in the GEN 2 guide until you finish step GUIDING THE UPPER BELT (GANTRY-RIGHT).

GEN 2 3. Belts upgrade steps 4–38 of 64 · Very difficult

Removing the belts

GEN 2 3.4 source ↗
  • Remove both belts from the assembly.
  • ReminderCaution: The belt tensioner idlers are still attached to the belts.

Releasing the left motor

GEN 2 3.5 source ↗
  • Move to the underside of the left rear motor.
  • Remove the four M3x35 screws securing the motor to the motor holder.
  • Remove the M3x6 screw securing the motor holder.
  • CautionAvoid removing the screws securing the rod holder.

Releasing the right motor

GEN 2 3.6 source ↗
  • Loosen the screw securing the main cable clip and leave it attached to the cable bundle.
  • CautionDo not move or reposition the Main-cable-clip on the cable bundle during the upgrade.
  • Move to the underside of the right rear motor.
  • Remove the four M3x35 screws securing the motor to the motor holder.
  • Remove the M3x6 screw securing the motor holder.
  • CautionAvoid removing the screws securing the rod holder.

Disassembling the right motor

GEN 2 3.7 source ↗
  • ReminderWe recommend protecting the heatbed during handling. An empty Prusament box is an ideal protective layer.
  • Focus on the rear-right motor.
  • Remove the motor from the motor holder.
  • Place the motor on the edge of the printer frame.
  • Using a 2.0 mm Allen key, loosen the two set screws securing the pulley.
  • Remove the pulley.
  • Carefully cut the zip tie securing the motor cable to the motor mount.
  • ReminderThis pulley will no longer be used. Set it aside or discard it to avoid confusing it with the new one.

New pulley: parts preparation (right motor)

GEN 2 3.8 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • T21-1.5GT pulley (1x)
  • 1.5GT belt (2x)
  • Pulley-offset-tool (1x)

Installing the new pulley (right motor)

GEN 2 3.9 source ↗
  • Rotate the motor shaft so that the flat faces you. Do not rotate the shaft any further.
  • Slide the new T21-1.5GT pulley onto the end of the shaft, with the set screw side facing the motor.
  • Insert the Pulley-offset-tool, with the side marked "Y", between the motor and the pulley to set the correct distance.
  • Press the pulley against the Pulley-offset-tool and tighten the set screw against the flat on the motor shaft.
  • Rotate the pulley and tighten the second set screw.

Inserting the lower belt (right motor)

GEN 2 3.10 source ↗
  • Remove the motor mount from the printer.
  • Take one of the belts and form a loop with the teeth facing inward.
  • Push the belt loop into the motor mount between the two lower idlers.
  • Viewed from the top, the belt loop should follow the circular cutout in the motor mount as closely as possible.

Securing the lower belt (right motor)

GEN 2 3.11 source ↗
  • ReminderThroughout the process, make sure the belt does not slip out of the assembly.
  • Place the motor mount onto the printer frame. The side with the two idlers must be facing down and towards you.
  • Insert the motor with the pulley into the belt loop inside the motor mount.
  • Fully seat the motor against the motor mount.
  • Orient it so that the motor cable faces outward (towards you).
  • Gently pull both ends of the belts to secure the belt loop around the pulley.

Guiding the lower belt (right motor)

GEN 2 3.12 source ↗
  • Grasp the belt coming from the left idler.
  • Route the belt around the idler from the left side and insert it into the motor mount.
  • On the opposite side, watch for the belt to come out through the opening and pull it through until approximately 15 cm (6 in) is sticking out.

Guiding the upper belt (right motor)

GEN 2 3.13 source ↗
  • Take the second new belt.
  • Route one end of the belt around the upper idler from the left side. Make sure the teeth face away from the idler.
  • From the opposite side, watch for the belt to come out through the opening.
  • Pull it through until approximately the same length of belt is sticking out - around 15 cm (6 in).
  • Pro tip: To prevent the belts from being accidentally pulled out, loosely secure their ends together with a zip tie.

Securing the motor cable (right motor)

GEN 2 3.14 source ↗
  • ReminderThroughout the process, make sure the belts do not slip out of the assembly.
  • Move the assembly closer to the rear corner of the printer.
  • Route the free ends of the belts toward the rear of the printer. Leave them loose for now.
  • Make sure the M3nN nut is still inserted in the motor mount and has not fallen out.
  • If the M3nN nut has fallen out, reinsert it fully into the part.
  • Route the motor cable through the cable channel, as shown in the picture.
  • Push the zip tie through the hole in the printed part.
  • Carefully secure the cable with the zip tie.

Fixing the right motor

GEN 2 3.15 source ↗
  • Rotate the motor assembly with the motor mount into the correct position. The belt pulleys must face the rear side of the printer.
  • The motor mount has a tab on the bottom side that must fit into the rectangular cutout in the frame.
  • From the inner side of the printer, check that the lower belt is seated on the pulley throught the hexa hole in the motor-mount.

Right motor screws: parts preparation

GEN 2 3.16 source ↗
  • For the followings steps, please prepare:
  • M3x35 screw (4x) you removed earlier
  • M3x6 screw (1x) you removed earlier
  • M3nS nut (1x) you removed earliermay have remained inserted from the outer side of the motor mount.
  • M3x10 screw (1x) you removed earlier

Tightening the right motor

GEN 2 3.17 source ↗
  • Secure the entire motor assembly from the bottom side of the frame using four M3x35 screws.
  • Finally, secure the motor mount with an M3x6 screw.
  • From the top side, behind the motor, attach the Main-cable-clip back to the motor mount using the pre-inserted M3x10 screw.

Securing the Bowden-guide

GEN 2 3.18 source ↗
Companion article: the Bowden-guide is not needed for the INDX conversion. You can leave it off once it is detached from the motor mount.
  • From the outer side of the motor mount, insert the M3nN nut if it is not already inserted.
  • Attach the Bowden-guide to the motor-mount using the M3x10 screw.

Disassembling the left motor

GEN 2 3.19 source ↗
  • Focus on the rear-left motor.
  • Rotate the motor assembly with the cable facing outward.
  • Carefully cut the zip tie. Be careful not to cut the cable.
  • Remove the motor from the motor-mount and remove the motor-mount from the printer.
  • Place the motor on the printer frame.
  • Using a 2.0 mm Allen key, loosen the two set screws securing the pulley.
  • Remove the pulley.
  • ReminderThis pulley will no longer be used. Set it aside or discard it to avoid confusing it with the new one.

New pulley: parts preparation (left motor)

GEN 2 3.20 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • T21-1.5GT pulley (1x)
  • Pulley-offset-tool (1x) you used it before

Belt routing overview

GEN 2 3.21 source ↗
  • ReminderBefore routing the belts, familiarize yourself with their path through the CoreXY mechanism.
  • The following diagrams show the routing of the upper and lower belts and their orientation within the assembly.
  • Upper belt path
  • Lower belt path
  • Do not perform any actions in this step.

Installing the new pulley (left motor)

GEN 2 3.22 source ↗
  • Rotate the motor shaft so that the flat faces you. Do not rotate the shaft any further.
  • Slide the new T21-1.5GT pulley onto the shaft, with the set screw side facing away from the motor.
  • Insert the Pulley-offset-tool, with the side marked "X", between the motor and the pulley to set the correct distance.
  • Press the pulley against the Pulley-offset-tool and tighten the set screw against the flat on the motor shaft.
  • Rotate the pulley and tighten the second set screw.

Guiding the lower belt (left motor)

GEN 2 3.23 source ↗
  • Route both belts from the right motor towards the rear side of the printer and guide them to the left motor.
  • Place the motor-mount onto the printer frame with the side containing one pulley facing downward.
  • Route the lower belt around the lower idler from the right side.
  • CautionMake sure you are holding the lower belt coming from the right motor.
    The belt must not be twisted along its path.
  • From the opposite side, pull the belt out approximately 15 cm (6 in).

Inserting the upper belt (left motor)

GEN 2 3.24 source ↗
  • Take the upper belt and form a loop with the teeth facing inward.
  • Push the belt loop into the motor mount between the two upper pulleys.
  • Viewed from the top, the belt loop should follow the circular cutout in the motor mount as closely as possible.

Securing the upper belt (left motor)

GEN 2 3.25 source ↗
  • ReminderThroughout the process, make sure the belt does not slip out of the assembly.
  • Insert the motor with the pulley into the belt loop inside the motor mount.
  • Fully seat the motor against the motor mount.
  • Orient it so that the motor cable faces backward (towards the pulleys).
  • Gently pull both ends of the belts to secure the belt loop around the pulley.

Guiding the upper belt (left motor)

GEN 2 3.26 source ↗
  • Grasp the right belt coming from the upper pulley.
  • Route the belt around the upper right pulley from the right side and insert it into the motor mount.
  • On the opposite side, watch for the belt to come out through the opening and pull it through until approximately 15 cm (6 in) is sticking out.

Securing the motor cable (left motor)

GEN 2 3.27 source ↗
  • Move the assembly closer to the rear corner of the printer.
  • Route the motor cable through the cable channel, as shown in the picture.
  • Push the zip tie through the hole in the printed part. And carefully secure the cable with the zip tie.

Fixing the left motor

GEN 2 3.28 source ↗
  • Rotate the motor assembly with the motor mount into the correct position. The belt idlers must face the rear side of the printer.
  • The motor mount has a tab on the bottom side that must fit into the rectangular cutout in the frame.
  • From the inner side of the printer, check that the upper belt is seated on the idler throught the hexa hole in the motor-mount.

Belt tensioner pulleys: parts preparation

GEN 2 3.29 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • M3x35 screw (4x) you removed earlier
  • M3x6 screw (1x) you removed earlier
  • Belt tensioner assembly (2x) you removed earlier

Tightening the left motor

GEN 2 3.30 source ↗
  • Secure the entire motor assembly from the bottom side of the frame using four M3x35 screws.
  • Finally, secure the motor mount with an M3x6 screw.

Guiding the upper belt (left side)

GEN 2 3.31 source ↗
  • Take the upper belt coming from the left motor.
  • Route the belt around the idler so that:
  • The "L" (left) mark on the idler faces upward
  • The toothed side of the belt does not contact the idler
  • CautionThe belt must not be twisted along its path.

Attaching the left belt tensioner

GEN 2 3.32 source ↗
  • Insert the idler with the belt wrapped around it into the "rails" of the left tensioner.
  • From the opposite side, tighten the pre-inserted screw until the idler assembly starts to move.
  • Stop tightening when the sliding part is flush with the stationary part.

Guiding the upper belt (gantry - left)

GEN 2 3.33 source ↗
  • Route the free end of the belt coming from the idler around the upper idler on the XY gantry.
  • NoteThe XY gantry idlers may differ visually between printer versions. The procedure is identical for both 3D-printed and injection-molded parts.

Guiding the lower belt (gantry - left)

GEN 2 3.34 source ↗
  • Take the lower belt coming from the left motor.
  • Route it towards the XY gantry and around the lower idler.
  • From the opposite side, pull the belt through until at least 8 cm (3 in) is sticking out.

Guiding the lower belt

GEN 2 3.35 source ↗
  • Move to the right motor.
  • Remove the zip tie securing the two free belt ends on the right side of the printer, if you used one.
  • Take the lower belt coming from the right motor.
  • Route the belt around the idler so that:
  • The "R" (right) mark on the idler faces upward
  • The toothed side of the belt does not contact the idler
  • CautionThe belt must not be twisted along its path.

Attaching the right belt tensioner

GEN 2 3.36 source ↗
  • Insert the idler with the belt wrapped around it into the "rails" of the right tensioner.
  • From the opposite side, tighten the pre-inserted screw until the idler assembly starts to move.
  • Stop tightening when the sliding part is flush with the stationary part.

Guiding the lower belt (gantry - right)

GEN 2 3.37 source ↗
  • Route the free end of the belt coming from the idler around the lower idler on the XY gantry.
  • From the opposite side, pull the belt through until at least 8 cm (3 in) is sticking out.
  • NoteThe XY gantry idlers may differ visually between printer versions. The procedure is identical for both 3D-printed and injection-molded parts.

Guiding the upper belt (gantry - right)

GEN 2 3.38 source ↗
  • Take the upper belt coming from the right motor.
  • Route the belt around the upper idler on the XY gantry.
  • From the opposite side, pull the belt through until at least 8 cm (3 in) is sticking out.
  • ReminderIf you are assembling the Prusa INDX along with the GEN 2 upgrade, return to the Prusa INDX GEN 2 article now.
