Gantry aligner tool

source ↗

Return to the Prusa INDX guide step GANTRY ALIGNER TOOL: PARTS PREPARATION, and continue from there.

  • You will notice that the right panel and side cover are still in place in the Prusa INDX guide for now. Proceed as if the right side cover and panel were removed in the Prusa INDX guide as well.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide all the way until you finish step COVERING THE FS - RIGHT.

INDX 4. INDX Toolhead & Side filament sensors steps 4–52 of 71 · Moderate

Gantry aligner tool: parts preparation

INDX 4.4 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-Gantry-aligner-tool (2x) found in the Position tools bag

Installing the Gantry-aligner-tool - right

INDX 4.5 source ↗
  • Start by slightly loosening three screws on the back of the gantry on each side.
  • Place one of the Gantry-aligner-tool on the front right side of the X-axis, aligning the linear rail with the matching cutout.
  • NoteBoth Gantry-aligner-tools are identical.
  • The fork must face the pulleys.
  • Slide the Gantry-aligner-tool fully onto the gantry frame profile, ensuring the cutouts engage.
  • Route both free belt ends through the open space above the tool.

Installing the Gantry-aligner-tool - left

INDX 4.6 source ↗
  • Place the Gantry-aligner-tool on the front left side of the X-axis, aligning the linear rail with the matching cutout.
  • The fork must face the pulleys.
  • Slide the Gantry-aligner-tool fully onto the gantry frame profile, engaging the cutouts.
  • Route both free belt ends through the open space above the tool.
  • With each Gantry-aligner-tool in place, tighten the three screws on each side of the back of the gantry.

Aligning the linear rail

INDX 4.7 source ↗
  • Using a 2.5 mm Allen key, loosen all six screws securing the linear rail.
  • Do not fully loosen the screw. 2–3 turns are sufficient.
  • Move the linear bearing back and forth along the full length of the axis.
  • Firmly tighten all six screws one by one in the specified order.

Removing the Gantry-aligner-tool

INDX 4.8 source ↗
  • Remove both Gantry-aligner-tools from the printer.
  • NoteThis part will no longer be needed.

Toolhead mount: parts preparation

INDX 4.9 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Head-mounting-plate (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
  • M3x8b screw (4x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3nS nut (2x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag

Securing the belts

INDX 4.10 source ↗
  • Hold the Head-mounting-plate in the correct orientation, using the protrusion as a guide.
  • From the right side, route the lower belt through the rear center opening in the Head-mounting-plate, around the post, and back out. It must extend 4–5 teeth.
  • Route the upper belt through the front center opening in the Head-mounting-plate, around the post, and back out. It must extend 4–5 teeth.
  • CautionMake sure the belts are not crossed.
  • Hold the right belts in place with your thumb to prevent them from slipping out.
  • Route the upper belt through the front center opening out (down) of the Head-mounting-plate. It must extend 6–7 teeth.
  • From the left side, route the lower belt through the rear center opening out (down) of the Head-mounting-plate. It must extend 6–7 teeth.
  • Insert the belt ends from the left side into the left opening and press them in. Leave 4–5 teeth protruding on from the rear side of the Head-mounting-plate.

Installing the Head-mounting-plate

INDX 4.11 source ↗
  • Double-check that all four belt ends protrude 4–5 teeth inward.
  • Insert two M3nS nuts into the protrusion of the Head-mounting-plate.
  • Place the Head-mounting-plate against the linear bearing and align it with the holes.
  • Using a 2.0 mm Allen key, secure the part with four M3x8b screws. Tighten the screws firmly, but gently.
  • CautionCheck on both sides that the belts are correctly routed through their channels and are not pinched anywhere.

Lubricating the belt tensioner screw

INDX 4.12 source ↗
SKIP. The companion article has you lubricate both M3x30 belt-tensioner screws earlier, during the Gen 2 belt exchange, and says to skip this step when it appears here.
  • If your printer is a Prusa CORE One, we will need to lubricate the belt tensioner screws.
  • NoteThis step does not apply if you have the Prusa CORE One+ version.
  • Prepare the Prusa lubricant (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag.
  • Apply a small amount of Prusa lubricant to the tip of both left and right M3x30 tensioning screws you removed earlier.
  • Spread the lubricant evenly around the entire thread.
  • ReminderTip: Use the tip of a zip tie to spread the lubricant.

Adjusting the belts

INDX 4.13 source ↗
  • Insert the lubricated tensioning screws in the front left and front right profiles.
  • Using a 2.5 mm Allen key, connect the Belt-tensioner-pulley to the Belt-tensioner.
  • Using the same process, connect the Belt-tensioner-pulley on the right side as well.
  • Tension the belts so that both tensioning mechanisms are in approximately the same position as shown in the picture - about 8 mm (0.31 in) from the edge of the tensioner.
  • NoteTypically, this requires 8–10 turns.
  • ReminderFinal fine-tuning will be done in the final chapter.

INDX Toolhead assembly: Parts preparation

INDX 4.14 source ↗
  • For the next step, prepare:
  • INDX Toolhead (1x) found in the INDX Toolhead box
  • Head cable cover front (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3x18 screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag

Attaching the head cable cover front

INDX 4.15 source ↗
  • Use the T10 key/screwdriver to remove two M3x6T screws.
  • Remove the INDX Toolhead cover.
  • Attach the head cable cover front to the INDX Toolhead.
  • Secure the head cable cover front with the M3x18 screw.
  • Carefully attach the INDX Toolhead cover. Ensure that no cables are pinched.
  • Secure the cover in place with the two M3x6T screws you removed earlier.
  • Ensure that the four highlighted holes are empty. If there are any screws, remove them before mounting the INDX Toolhead later on.

INDX Toolhead: parts preparation

INDX 4.16 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX Toolhead (1x) that you assembled earlier
  • M3x14 screw (4x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag

Mounting the INDX Toolhead

INDX 4.17 source ↗
  • From the rear side of the Head-mounting-plate, insert two M3x14 screws into the holes.
  • From the front side, place the INDX Toolhead onto the Head-mounting-plate as shown in the picture.
  • Secure it using the upper M3x14 screws and fully tighten them firmly.
  • Secure the INDX Toolhead by inserting two M3x14 screws into the lower holes and tightening them firmly.
  • CautionWARNING: Avoid contact with the front metal LED holder to prevent damage or scratches to the INDX Toolhead.

Fan shroud: parts preparation

INDX 4.18 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • INDX-C1-Fan-shroud (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
  • M3x14 screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3nS nut (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag

Attaching the Fan-shroud

INDX 4.19 source ↗
  • Attach the Fan-shroud to the INDX toolhead from below.
  • Note the ridge in the Fan-shroud. This ridge will slide onto the bottom part of the Head-mounting-plate.
  • Secure the Fan-shroud using the M3x14 screw from the right side.
  • Secure it from the left side using an M3x14 screw as well.

Inserting the nut

INDX 4.20 source ↗
  • Insert an M3nS nut into the protrusion on the left side of the INDX Toolhead.
  • From the front, check through the screw hole that the nut is properly seated.

Print fan: parts preparation

INDX 4.21 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Print fan (1x) removed earlier
  • M3x25 screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • NoteIn case you converted your CORE One from the MK4/S printer, the cable on your print fan is much longer. Use the supplied Print fan blower (1x) found in the Electronics box here instead.
  • The print fan you removed from your converted printer will be used in substitution for the Dock fan later on.

Installing the print fan

INDX 4.22 source ↗
  • Look at the INDX Toolhead from the rear side.
  • Take the print fan as shown and align it with the Fan-shroud opening.
  • Insert the print fan into the Fan-shroud opening.
  • Secure it with one M3x25 screw.
  • CautionDo not overtighten the screw to avoid cracking the fan housing.
  • Guide the print fan cable under the cable hook on the Fan-shroud.

Connecting the print fan

INDX 4.23 source ↗
  • Plug the print fan cable into the connector in the INDX Toolhead.
  • Keep the cable from protruding too far to the side.

INDX head cable: parts preparation I.

INDX 4.24 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Head-cable-clip (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
  • Swingarm-clip found in the Toolhead bag
  • Head cable cover back (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3x10 screw (1x) you removed earlier
  • M3x8rT screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • 3x8sT black screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag

INDX head cable: parts preparation II.

INDX 4.25 source ↗
  • INDX head cable (1x) found in the Cables bag
  • Nylon string 4 x 2.5 x 450 (1x) found in the INDX Fasteners and Plastic parts box
  • Cable tie (2x) you removed earlier

Guiding the head cable

INDX 4.26 source ↗
  • Now move to the rear side of the printer.
  • Pass the head cable connector through the lower oval opening on the left side of the rear panel.
  • NoteSome of our printers do not have the grommet on the lower opening. This does not affect the process.
  • Insert most of the braided cable into the printer.The exact length will be adjusted later.
  • ReminderMake sure the grommet does not slide into the printer. If needed, you can pull it outward for easier handling; it will be reinstalled later.
  • Inside the printer, route the head cable upward through the corner behind the gantry assembly.

Inserting the nylon string

INDX 4.27 source ↗
  • In this step, we will insert the nylon into the cable sleeve.
  • Insert the nylon string into the cable sleeve near the head cable connector.
  • CautionEnsure that the nylon string is inserted as shown, with the end of the nylon pointing down.
  • ReminderEnsure that the nylon string is completely wrapped inside the sleeve, along with the head cable.
  • Continue inserting the nylon string into the cable sleeve along the whole length.
  • Leave the end of the nylon string sticking out from the cable sleeve as shown, with the end of the nylon pointing down.
  • Tighten the cable sleeve around the head cable and the nylon string by gently twisting the sleeve.

Connecting the head cable

INDX 4.28 source ↗
  • Plug the head cable into the INDX Toolhead. Ensure that the safety latch clicks in place.
  • Insert the nylon string into the slot in the head cable cover front. Ensure that the nylon is inserted all the way in.
  • Insert the cables into the channel. Ensure that no cables are sticking out.
  • Adjust the textile sleeve so that 1.5 cm (0.59 in) is inside the channel.
  • Note the protruding bit on the head cable cover back. It will fit into the slot in the INDX Toolhead.
  • Attach the head cable cover back.
  • CautionWhen attaching the Head-cable-cover, ensure you do not pinch or damage any cables.
  • Use the 3x8sT self-tapping black screw to secure the Head-cable-cover in place.

Attaching the head cable

INDX 4.29 source ↗
  • Gently open up the Swing-arm-clip and attach it to the head cable with the nylon inside of the cable sleeve.
  • CautionProceed carefully. Do not break the Swing-arm-clip when attaching it to the head cable.
  • Pay attention to the correct orientation; the protruding side of the clip and the side with the cut-out for the screw must face the front of the printer.
  • Once the Swing-arm-clip is on the head cable, adjust it so the distance between the clip and the bend in the nylon is 1.4 cm / 0.55 inch
  • Locate the rightmost narrowing on the swing arm. We will mount the Swing-arm-clip there in the next step.
  • Note the hole in the swing arm. This is where we will insert the nylon end in the next step.

Securing the swing arm clip

INDX 4.30 source ↗
  • Attach the Swing-arm-clip to the swing arm from the top. Ensure that the clip is placed on the rightmost narrowing on the swing arm.
  • Insert the end of the nylon into the hole in the swingarm.
  • ReminderEnsure that the cable sleeve is not pinched where the nylon is sticking out.
  • With the Swing-arm-clip and the nylon in the correct positions, secure the clip in place with the M3x8rT screw.

Securing the head cable

INDX 4.31 source ↗
  • Wrap the cable tie around the head cable and the middle narrowing of the swing arm.
  • Tighten the cable tie and wrap the excess strap around it.
  • Secure the head cable with the cable tie around the leftmost narrowing on the Swing arm.

Installing the Head cable clip

INDX 4.32 source ↗
  • Make sure that the cable sleeve is tightly wrapped around the cables. Twist the cable sleeve slightly to tighten it.
  • Carefully open the Head-cable-clip and attach it to the head cable.
  • ReminderPay attention to the correct orientation, using the "X" symbol and the cutout for the screw head as a guide.
  • Align the Head-cable-clip with the hole on the Y motor mount protrusion.
  • Secure the part using an M3x10 screw.
  • NotePro tip: Pre-thread the M3x10 screw into the part after snapping it onto the cable.

Connecting the head cable: parts preparation

INDX 4.33 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Zip tie (3x)

Inserting the zip ties

INDX 4.34 source ↗
  • Pass the zip tie through the upper perforation in the xBuddy box. The zip tie must run underneath all cables.
  • Do the same for the other two perforations.

Connecting the head cable

INDX 4.35 source ↗
  • Guide the head cable through the left opening in the xBuddy box.
  • Plug the branched head cable connector as follows:
  • Narrow connector: plug it into the MMU-labeled slot on the xBuddy Extension board.
  • Wide connector: plug it into the Nextruder-labeled slot on the xBuddy board.

Securing the cables

INDX 4.36 source ↗
  • Adjust the cable management according to the picture. Route all cables along the edges.
  • Tighten the zip ties on the right side and trim the excess.
  • CautionDo not overtighten to avoid damaging the cables.
  • Leave the last connector of the head cable unplugged. This will be done later on when we connect the dock fan.
  • We recommend hanging the cable on the other cables so it does not get damaged when turning the printer.

Haribo time!

INDX 4.37 source ↗
  • ReminderTime for a little yummy gummy break.
  • Take a small reward break: eat five gummy bears.

INDX PTFE holders: parts preparation

INDX 4.38 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will only need the left PTFE holder and one screw.
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-PTFE-holder-left (1x) marked “L” found in the Filament Holder Left bag
  • INDX-PTFE-holder-right (1x) marked “R”  found in the Filament Holder Right bag
  • M3x10 screw (2x) you removed earlier

Installing the PTFE-holder-left

INDX 4.39 source ↗
  • Using the 2.5mm Allen key release and remove two M3x4 screws securing the top rear profile.
  • Take the PTFE-holder-left and insert one M3x10 screw.
  • Align the PTFE-holder-left with the left hole on the top rear profile.
  • Join both parts by fully tightening the M3x10 screw.

Installing the PTFE-holder-right

INDX 4.40 source ↗
  • NoteSkip this step if you have the 4-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX.
  • Take the PTFE-holder-right and insert one M3x10 screw.
  • Align the PTFE-holder-right with the right hole on the rear profile.
  • Join both parts by fully tightening the M3x10 screw.
  • Visually compare both PTFE holders with the picture.

Side filament sensors: parts preparation

INDX 4.41 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-C1-FS-top (1x) found in the Filament holder L bag
  • INDX-C1-FS-top (1x) found in the Filament holder R bag
  • NoteNote that each part has a different position numbering.
  • Sleeve 2x5 (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
  • Collet (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
  • M3x12cT screw (4x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • Magnet 3.2 x 5 (4x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag

Inserting the sleeves

INDX 4.42 source ↗
  • Insert the 2x5 sleeves into the indicated positions in the square opening of the FS-top.
  • Push each sleeve fully into place using a non-sharp tool. It will click when correctly seated.
  • Check from the side that each sleeve is in the correct position:
  • The sleeve is in the correct position.
  • The sleeve needs to be pushed further.
  • Repeat this procedure for all the sleeves on both FS-top parts.

Inserting the collets

INDX 4.43 source ↗
  • Position the FS-top with the square openings facing down.
  • Insert the collets into the top openings.
  • Use this procedure for both FS-top parts.

Installing the magnets

INDX 4.44 source ↗
  • Insert the 5x2 magnet into the FS-top with the cut-out facing up.
  • Secure the magnet with the M3x12cT screw.
  • NoteThe magnet may stick to the T10 key during tightening; hold it in place by hand.
  • Repeat the same process to install the remaining magnets on both FS-top parts.

Assembling the FS: parts preparation I

INDX 4.45 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • Magnet 7x8 (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
  • Steelball 7mm (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag.

Assembling the FS: parts preparation II

INDX 4.46 source ↗
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • INDX-C1-FS-holder (1x) found in the Filament holder L bag
  • INDX-C1-FS-holder (1x) found in the Filament holder R bag
  • Filament sensor board Left (1x) found in the electronics box
  • Filament sensor board Right (1x) found in the electronics box
  • M3x12cT screw (8x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • NoteBoth INDX-C1-FS-holders are identical. If you have the 4-tool version, you only received the left Filament sensor board with two connectors.

Inserting the steel balls

INDX 4.47 source ↗
  • Insert one steelball 7mm into each round hole.
  • Repeat the process with the second FS-top part.

Attaching the magnets

INDX 4.48 source ↗
  • NoteThe magnets are quite strong. Make sure that you keep both parts far from each other.
  • Place one of the 7x8 magnets onto the 5x2 magnet. Note which side attracts the magnet.
  • Insert the magnet in the same hole as you placed the steelball 7mm.
  • CautionMake sure that you insert the magnet with the attracting side going first.
  • Check that you have the correct position of the magnets:
  • NOT OK: When the magnet is poking out, it needs to be flipped and inserted again correctly.
  • OK: The magnet is seated in the hole.

Assembling the FS-top left

INDX 4.49 source ↗
  • Prepare the FS-top assembly (positions 4–1).
  • Insert the filament sensor board LEFT (with two connectors) into the ridge in the filament sensor holder top.
  • Make sure the connectors are correctly oriented relative to the printed part.
  • Insert the part fully down.
  • Secure the part using two M3x12cT countersunk screws.

Covering the FS - left

INDX 4.50 source ↗
  • Place the FS-holder onto the filament sensor assembly, ensuring the connectors pass through the rectangular opening.
  • Use the two M3x12cT screws to secure the board in place. Tighten them firmly.
  • NoteIf you have the 4-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX, skip to this step: PTFE tubes - left side: parts preparation

Assembling the FS-top right

INDX 4.51 source ↗
  • Prepare the FS-top assembly with the (positions 8–5).
  • Insert the filament sensor board RIGHT (with one connector) into the ridge in the filament sensor holder top.
  • Make sure the connector are correctly oriented relative to the printed part.
  • Insert the part fully down.
  • Secure the part using two M3x12cT countersunk screws.

Covering the FS - right

INDX 4.52 source ↗
  • Prepare the filament sensor assembly right (positions 8-5).
  • Place the FS-holder onto the filament sensor assembly, ensuring the connector pass through the rectangular opening.
  • Use the two M3x12cT screws to secure the board in place. Tighten them firmly.
  • ReminderIf you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, return to the Prusa INDX GEN 2 article now.

Mounting the side panels, PTFE and right cover

source ↗

Before you move on to the next step in the Prusa INDX guide, we need to attach both of the top see-through side panels.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Use four nylon rivets to reattach the left top see-through side cover. Do not insert a nylon rivet into the top middle hole. This is where we will mount the filament sensor in the Prusa INDX guide later.
  • Mount the right top see-through side cover. If you have the 8-tool version of the Prusa CORE One INDX, do not insert the top-middle nylon rivet as well.

With both top see-through covers mounted back, continue following the Prusa INDX guide step PTFE TUBES - LEFT SIDE: PARTS PREPARATION, and continue from there.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE ZIP TIES II.

INDX 4. INDX Toolhead & Side filament sensors steps 53–71 of 71 · Moderate

PTFE tubes - left side: parts preparation

INDX 4.53 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you only need one cable.
  • For the following steps, please prepare:
  • Filament sensor cable (2x) found in the Cables bag
  • 3x12sT screw (2x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • PTFE tube 4 x 2.5 x 880 (4x) found in the main box

Preparing the FS - left

INDX 4.54 source ↗
  • Remove the upper center nylon rivet from the left transparent side panel.
  • Insert a 3x12sT screw from the inside into the rivet hole.
  • Take the filament sensor assembly with the two connectors (positions 4–1) and connect the two filament sensor cables to it.
  • NoteThe 4-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX has one filament sensor cable. Plug it into any of the connectors.
  • NoteBoth ends of the filament sensor cable are identical and can be connected interchangeably.
  • Guide the cables out through the cable channels on the left side.

Mounting the FS - left

INDX 4.55 source ↗
  • Align the left filament sensor assembly with the protruding 3x12sT screw.
  • Ensure correct orientation - the collets must face upward.
  • Fully tighten the screw to secure the assembly. Make sure that:
  • The tab along the top edge is seated in the gap above the transparent side panel.

Connecting the PTFE tube - left

INDX 4.56 source ↗
  • Insert both filament sensor cables into the lower cable channels in the PTFE-holder.
  • NoteThe 4-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX has one filament sensor cable. Lead it through the bottom channel.
  • The cables should neither sag nor be under tension along the route.
  • Insert four PTFE tubes into the collets in the filament sensor.
  • Once inserted, try to gently pull the tube out of the collet to verify it is locked in.

PTFE measurement: parts preparation

INDX 4.57 source ↗
  • For the following parts, please prepare:
  • Prusa Cheatsheet (1x)
  • NoteIt is on the reverse side of the welcome letter you received at the beginning of the package.
  • Filament 300 mm (2x)
  • ReminderCut two pieces of filament at least 300 mm long. We recommend using PETG, but it's not required.
  • NoteIf you have a 300 mm gauge, you can use it as an alternative.
  • INDX-PTFE-holder-cover (1x) found in the Filament holder left bag
  • M3x10 screw (2x) you removed earlier

Attaching the PTFE tubes - left

INDX 4.58 source ↗
  • Insert two M3x10 screws through the INDX-PTFE-holder-cover and keep the part nearby.
  • Guide all four PTFE tubes through the channels in the PTFE-holder. Hold them in place by hand to prevent them from falling out.
  • CautionMake sure the filament sensor cables are routed in the lower channels.
  • Place the PTFE-holder-cover over the PTFE tubes and the cables. The part is not symmetrical, install it with the longer side facing down.
  • Do not fully tighten it; the PTFE tubes must be able to move back and forth.

Measurement info

INDX 4.59 source ↗
  • ReminderIn the following steps, you will measure the correct PTFE tube length between the PTFE-holder and the filament sensor.
  • You can either use a measuring tape or the filament method described below:
  • Along the side of the Prusa Cheatsheet you received with your Prusa CORE One/+ INDX, note the scale in millimeters - these indicate the required PTFE tube lengths.
  • The initial length is 300 mm. Do not shorten it yet.
  • NoteIn the following steps, you will be instructed to shorten the filament to the required length.
  • If you have the 8-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX, keep the second piece of filament for the right side.

Inserting the PTFE tubes (position 1,2)

INDX 4.60 source ↗
  • Place one end of the filament at the filament sensor against the PTFE tube at position 1.
  • Place the other end against the same PTFE tube at the PTFE-holder.
  • Slide the filament in the PTFE-holder to match the PTFE tube length.
  • ReminderCut the filament to 270 mm.
  • Adjust the PTFE tube to position 2 according to the shortened filament.
  • Fully tighten the upper screw.
  • NoteThis will lock the first PTFE tubes in place and prevent movement.

Inserting the PTFE tubes (position 3,4)

INDX 4.61 source ↗
  • ReminderCut the filament to 240 mm.
  • Adjust the PTFE tube to position 3 according to the shortened filament.
  • ReminderCut the filament to 210 mm.
  • Adjust the PTFE tube to position 4 according to the shortened filament.
  • Fully tighten the lower screw.
  • NoteIf you have the 4-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX, skip to this step: Connecting the filament sensor cable

INDX 4.62 source ↗

  • M3x10 screw (2x) you removed earlier

Mounting the FS - right

INDX 4.64 source ↗
  • Align the right filament sensor assembly with the protruding 3x12sT screw.

INDX 4.66 source ↗
  • Insert two M3x10 screws through the INDX-PTFE-holder-cover and keep the part nearby.

INDX 5.10 source ↗

  • NotePro tip: Lightly wipe the wiper blocks with IPA (Isopropyl alcohol) before inserting and securing them in the wiper base. This will make the insertion a lot easier.

GEN 2 4. Heatbed upgrade steps 11–20 of 42 · Moderate

Expansion joint aligner

GEN 2 4.11 source ↗
  • Prepare the Expansion-joint-aligner for the following steps.
  • NoteYour package includes the black version. The orange version is shown in this guide for better visibility.
  • In the following steps, you will precisely align each expansion joint.
  • For reference, see the second image showing the simplified aligner orientation for a single expansion joint.
  • The third image shows the alignment tool being slid onto the expansion joint for reference.
  • NoteThe expansion joint is shown outside the printer for clarity. During alignment, it is installed under the heatbed.

Aligning the front side expansion joint

GEN 2 4.12 source ↗
  • Insert the M3x4cT screws into all eight holes around the heatbed. Tighten each screw by one turn only.
  • Start by aligning the middle expansion joint on the front side.
  • NoteUse the symbols on the heatbed as a reference.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the front left expansion joint

GEN 2 4.13 source ↗
  • Move to the left corner.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the left side expansion joint

GEN 2 4.14 source ↗
  • Move to the left side of the heatbed.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the rear left expansion joint

GEN 2 4.15 source ↗
  • Move to the rear left corner.
  • Slide the angled fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the middle rear expansion joint

GEN 2 4.16 source ↗
  • Continue with the middle rear expansion joint.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the rear right expansion joint

GEN 2 4.17 source ↗
  • Continue with the rear right corner.
  • Slide the angled fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the right side expansion joint

GEN 2 4.18 source ↗
  • Move to the right side of the heatbed.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Aligning the front right expansion joint

GEN 2 4.19 source ↗
  • Continue with the front right corner.
  • NoteIf you are converting your printer to the Prusa INDX version, move the offset sensor out of the way to align this expansion joint, then place it back.
  • Slide the straight fork onto the expansion joint and push the Expansion-joint-aligner against the heatbed. This will align the expansion joint.
  • Push the aligner firmly against the edge of the heatbed.
  • Tighten the screw, but just lightly.

Fixing the heatbed

GEN 2 4.20 source ↗
  • CautionIMPORTANT: The heatbed must be tightened in a specific order. Repeat the sequence multiple times, ensuring the final tightening after at least two rounds.
  • After all screws are in place, tighten them in the following sequence:

  • Center screw
  • First fours screw (edges)
  • Last four screws (corners)
  • Tighten the screws gently, but firmly.
  • Double-check that the expansion joint has not rotated and that the groove is facing outwards from the printer.
  • ReminderIf you are assembling the Prusa INDX along with the GEN 2 upgrade,  return to the Prusa INDX GEN 2 article now.
COMPANION ARTICLE

Mounting the left cover, covering the electronics

source ↗

Now that the expansion joints are aligned, let's return to the step we skipped in the Prusa INDX guide and secure the offset sensor assembly by tightening the M3x10 screw.

The screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Do not overtighten.

  • You will notice that the right-side cover is still in place in the photo above. Proceed as if it were not there; it does not affect the process.

Once the heatbed is secured and the expansion joints are aligned, we can connect the X and Y motor cables and mount the left-side cover.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Connect the left motor cable (X motor) to the left connector on the xBuddy board. It is labeled X.
  • Connect the right motor cable (Y motor) to the right connector on the xBuddy board. It is labeled Y.
  • Make sure that the safety latches click in place.

  • Mount the left side panel back onto the printer. Secure it in place with 3 nylon rivets in the highlighted positions.

Once the left side cover is secured in place with three nylon rivets, we are finished with the CORE One GEN 2 guide.

Return to the Prusa INDX guide to step ELECTRONICS COVERS: PARTS PREPARATION and follow the rest of the Prusa INDX guide to finish the conversion.

  • Install another Puck holder top onto the next Puck-universal part, but in a mirrored orientation.
  • If you have the 8 tool version, assemble the second pair of the Puck holder top parts using the same process.

Tilting the printer

INDX 5.46 source ↗
  • NotePictured is the 8-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX with bottom-right puck holders and the right filament sensors included.
  • Remove the Prusament box from the heatbed and place it behind the printer.
  • Move the toolhead to the back of the printer.
  • Place all the PTFE tubes inside the printer.
  • Place the box behind the printer and slowly and carefully lay the printer down so it can lean on the box.
  • CautionEnsure that the printer is stable and that it can not slide or fall when tilted. We recommend asking someone to hold the printer while it rests on the box to ensure your safety.
  • Ensure that the filament sensor cables are not pinched.

Dock fan: parts preparation

INDX 5.59 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Dock-fan-holder (1x) found in the Toolhead bag
  • Print fan blower (1x) found in the Electronics box
  • Dock fan splitter board (1x) found in the Electronics box
  • M3x25 screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 1/2 bag
  • M3nS nut (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • M3x8rT screw (1x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • M3x35 screw (2x) found in the Tool Dock Fan bag

Assembling the dock fan

INDX 5.60 source ↗
  • Insert the M3nS nut into the Dock-fan-holder.
  • Insert the two M3x35 screws into the Dock-fan-holder. Do this before attaching the dock fan.
  • Insert the print fan. Ensure that the orientation of the fan is as shown in the photo.
  • The highlighted holes have to align once the fan is inserted.
  • Secure the fan in the Dock-fan-holder with the M3x25 screw.

Attaching the Dock fan splitter board

INDX 5.61 source ↗
  • Flip the dock fan assembly so that the sticker on the dock fan is visible.
  • Note the highlighted area.
  • Place the Dock fan splitter board into the ridge in the Dock-fan-holder. Ensure that the hole in the board aligns with the hole in the holder.
  • NoteBefore you touch the electronics, touch any conductive (metal) surface to neutralize the static charge from your hands.
  • Always touch the sides of the board only while handling it. Avoid touching the components on the surface.
  • Secure the Dock fan splitter board in place with the M3x8rT screw.
  • Plug the dock fan cable into the slot that is closer to the fan. Ensure that the safety latch clicks in place.

Attaching the dock fan

INDX 5.62 source ↗
  • Remove the two highlighted M3x30 screws from the Belt-tensioner.
  • Do not remove the third screw.
  • Plug the dock fan cable connector into the remaining slot on the FunFan board. Make sure that the safety latch clicks in place.
  • NoteBe careful not to scratch or damage the printer with the two screws protruding from the dock fan assembly.

Securing the dock fan

INDX 5.63 source ↗
  • With the dock fan cable plugged in, carefully turn the dock fan assembly.
  • Gently lower the dock fan assembly to insert both M3x35 screws into the Belt-tensioner as shown.
  • With the dock fan in place, use the 2.5mm Allen key to tighten the two M3x35 screws.

Tooldock: parts preparation

INDX 5.65 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • INDX-Tool-holder (8x) found in the Tools bag
  • Thimble (8x) found in Tools bag
  • Spring 0.5 x 8.5 x 30 x 15 (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
  • Spring 0.63 x 5 x 15 x 11 (16x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX bag
  • M3x12cT countersunk screw (16x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag
  • INDX C1 Front profile (1x) found in the main box

Assembling the tool holder

INDX 5.66 source ↗
  • Fully thread the M3x12cT screw into both holes of the Tool-holder, then remove the screw.
  • NoteThis creates a thread in the part, making the Tool-holder easier to install on the front profile later.
  • Position the Tool-holder with the countersunk holes facing up.
  • Insert each Thimble into the oval hole in part Tool-holder.
  • Insert a large spring (0.5 x 8.5 x 30 x 15) into each Thimble.
  • Insert two small springs (0.63 x 5 x 15 x 11) into the side holes of part Tool-holder.
  • Repeat the same procedure for all remaining Tool-holder parts.

Installing the tool holders

INDX 5.67 source ↗
  • In the correct orientation, place the Tool-holder against position 1 on the underside of the front profile.
  • Align the holes in both parts.
  • CautionCAUTION: When placing the Tool-holder, make sure no spring is pinched against the front profile.
  • Secure the Tool-holder using two M3x12cT screws.
  • NoteThe screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Slight resistance is expected.
  • Grasp the Tool-holder and gently wiggle it. It must not be rigid - a slight, barely perceptible looseness is required.
  • ReminderRepeat the procedure for the remaining Tool-holder assemblies on the front profile, ideally in order 1–4, then 8–5 for easier handling.

Nozzle seal holder: parts preparation

INDX 5.68 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Nozzle-seal-holder (4x) found in the Tools bag
  • Nozzle parking plate (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX
  • Nozzle seal (8x) found in the Fasteners Tools INDX
  • M3x8rT screw (16x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag

Assembling the nozzle seal

INDX 5.69 source ↗
  • Slide a nozzle seal (silicone sleeve) onto each nozzle parking plate.
  • CautionCAUTION: Handle with care! The edges of the nozzle parking plate are sharp and may cause injury.

Assembling the Nozzle-seal-holder

INDX 5.70 source ↗
  • CautionNote the correct placement of the nozzle seal before attaching it to the Nozzle-seal-holder.
  • In the correct position, the holes align while the nozzle seal on the opposite side does not extend beyond the Nozzle-seal-holder.
  • Place the nozzle seal assembly onto the Nozzle-seal-holder so that the bent part of the Nozzle seal faces upward.
  • Attach the nozzle seal assembly to the Nozzle-seal-holder using an M3x8rT screw.
  • NoteTurn all the Nozzle-seal-holders upside down; this is how we will install them in the next step. The bent part of the nozzle seal is now facing downward. 
  • Install two nozzle seals on each Nozzle-seal-holder using the same method.

Installing the nozzle parking plates

INDX 5.71 source ↗
  • NoteWith the 4-toohlead version, start installing the nozzle holders from the same side as in the photo. Check the other side of the tooldock to ensure that you start from number 1.
  • Align the nozzle holder assembly with the holes at positions 1–2 on the front profile.
  • Ensure the nozzle seals are correctly oriented by matching the bent ends to the illustration.
  • From the other side, secure the nozzle seal holder assembly with two M3x8rT screws and tighten firmly.
  • NoteThe screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Slight resistance is expected.
  • CautionEnsure that none of the nozzle parking plates are bent or damaged during the assembly. 
  • Continue installing the remaining nozzle holder assemblies using the same method.

  • INDX-C1-Vent-lever-holder (1x)

  • M3x8rT screw (3x) found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag

Assembling the ventilation lever

INDX 5.73 source ↗
  • Place the Vent-idler onto the Vent-lever-holder in the same orientation.
  • Secure it with an M3x8rT screw.
  • Place an M3 washer under the screw.
  • From the inner side of the front profile, align the part with the two holes.
  • Note the “TOP” marking on the Vent-lever-holder. It must face upward toward the bent section of the front profile.
  • From the opposite side (front) secure it with two M3x8rT screws.

INDX 5.79 source ↗
  • Insert the INDX-C1-cover-latch into the top cover from the bottom. Note the orientation of the cover latch.
  • Insert the INDX-C1-cover-latch into the top cover from the bottom. Note the orientation of the cover latch.

  • ReminderDo not overtighten the screw. The lock must be able to turn.

  • Secure the top cover back in place with two nylon rivets.

Attaching the hinge base - left

INDX 5.82 source ↗
  • Place the Hinge-base near the front left hole in the top cover back.
  • Note that each Hinge-base part indicates which side it goes to. Ensure that the part is marked with an L (left).
  • Insert the 3x12sT screw from inside the printer and hold it in position.
  • Align the hole in the Hinge-base with the 3x12sT screw and connect the Hinge-base to the printer.

  • Note that each Hinge-base part indicates which side it goes to. Ensure that the part is marked with an L (left).

Attaching the top cover I.

INDX 5.84 source ↗

  • Insert one M3x25 screw with the spring into each hinge from the inner side.

Attaching the top cover II.

INDX 5.85 source ↗
  • Use an Allen key to tighten the M3x25 screw on the left hinge. Do not tighten it completely.
  • Use an Allen key to tighten the M3x25 screw on the right hinge. Do not tighten it completely.
  • Slowly open the top cover all the way.
  • Make sure that the spring is able to retract and expand when opening the lid. This will hold the top cover open.
  • NoteIf the top cover does not stay open, check the tightness of the two M3x25 screws in the hinges and make sure the spring is in place.

  • M3x4rT screw (2x) that were removed earlier
  • INDX Nozzle tool (8x) found in the INDX Nozzle tool box
  • CautionWarning: Avoid touching or damaging the rectangular sensing area on the INDX Nozzle tool. Fingerprints, grease, or any damage can affect temperature readings and cause print issues.

Attaching the tooldock

INDX 5.87 source ↗
  • Remove the two M3x4rT screws that hold the LED panel in place. Set the two screws aside; we will need them in the next step.
  • CautionSupport the LED panel with your hand when removing the screws, so it does not fall. Do not touch the LEDs and resistors on the LED strip!
  • Gently lean the LED panel on the left side of the printer.
  • Make sure that the LED cable is not damaged or pulled too hard during these steps.
  • Mount the assembled tooldock.
  • The left side of the tooldock has to be placed under the top profile.
  • The right side of the tooldock has to be placed above the top profile.

Securing the tooldock

INDX 5.88 source ↗
  • Secure the tooldock to the top profiles with one M3x4 screw on each side.
  • Secure the tooldock to the front of the printer with two M3x4rT screws (in the top holes).
  • Use the two M3x4rT screws you removed in the previous step to secure the lower part of the tooldock.

Attaching the LED panel

INDX 5.89 source ↗
  • Mount the LED panel onto the inner side of the tooldock. Do not touch the LEDs and resistors on the LED strip!
  • NoteThe LED cable should reach the new position of the LED panel. If the cable is too short, gently and slowly pull on it to make it the correct length.
  • Use two nylon rivets to secure the LED panel in place.
  • Close the top cover.

Optional: Installing the Buddy3D Camera

INDX 5.90 source ↗
  • NoteThis step is only required if you have a Buddy3D Camera.
  • Now is the right time to mount the camera in the front-left corner of the printer.
  • Use the dedicated installation guide:  Buddy3D Camera for CORE One Installation
  • NoteThe guide shows installation on the CORE One, but the procedure is the same. The camera attaches magnetically to the upper profiles of the printer.

Connecting the INDX Nozzle tools (positions 1–4)

INDX 5.91 source ↗
  • Insert the PTFE tubes through the openings on the back of the lid, keeping the correct order.
  • Insert the PTFE tube from position 1 into the first opening from the right.
  • Repeat the same process for the remaining positions. Always make sure each PTFE tube is routed through the matching opening in the lid.
  • Open the top lid.
  • From the inside, fully insert the PTFE tube from the first opening into the INDX Nozzle Tool at position 1.
  • NoteTry gently pulling the tube out of the collet to verify that it is locked in.
  • Repeat the same procedure for all tools in positions 1–4.

Docking the tools (positions 1–4)

INDX 5.92 source ↗
  • Place the INDX Nozzle tool on the first PTFE tube onto tool dock position 1 and align the magnetic pins on the tool with the openings in the tool dock.
  • Snap the INDX Nozzle tool into tool dock position 1.
  • CautionMake sure both pins snap in fully and the tool sits perfectly flush.
  • Repeat the same procedure for the remaining tools up to position 4.
  • ReminderDouble-check that the nozzle parking plates are in the correct position to seal the INDX Nozzle tool.
  • NoteIf you have the 4-tool version, skip to this step: Checking the tubes

Connecting the INDX Nozzle tools (positions 5–8)

INDX 5.93 source ↗
  • Close the top lid. Insert the PTFE tubes through the openings on the back of the lid, keeping the correct order.
  • Insert the PTFE tube from position 8 into the first opening from the left.
  • Repeat the same process for the remaining positions. Always make sure each PTFE tube is routed through the matching opening in the lid.
  • Open the top lid.
  • Insert the PTFE tube from the rightmost opening into the INDX Nozzle Tool at position 8.
  • NoteTry to gently pull the tube out to verify it is locked in the collet.
  • Repeat the same procedure for all tools in positions 8–5.

Docking the tools (positions 5–8)

INDX 5.94 source ↗
  • Place the INDX Nozzle tool on the last PTFE tube onto tool dock position 8 and align the magnetic pins on the tool with the openings in the tool dock.
  • Snap the INDX Nozzle tool into tool dock position 8.
  • CautionMake sure both pins snap in fully and the tool sits perfectly flush.
  • Repeat the same procedure for the remaining tools up to position 5.
  • NoteDouble-check that the nozzle parking plates are in the correct position to seal the INDX Nozzle tool.

Checking the tubes

INDX 5.95 source ↗
  • NotePictured is the 8-toolhead version.
  • CautionCheck that the PTFE tubes are not swapped and that each tube is correctly routed to the corresponding tool position.
  • You can now close the lid and secure it by rotating the locks by 90°.
  • NoteThis is optional at this stage, as the lid will need to be opened again later during calibration.
  • Remove the empty cardboard box from the printer, as it will no longer be needed.

Offset sensor cover: parts preparation

INDX 5.96 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Offset sensor sticker (1x) found in the Tool Dock Fan bag
  • NoteThe color of the offset sensor sticker might differ, but it does not affect the functionality.

Covering the offset sensor

INDX 5.97 source ↗
  • Peel the protective layer off the offset sensor sticker and gently place the sticker onto the offset sensor.
  • Ensure that the sticker covers the whole sensor.

Door panel: parts preparation

INDX 5.98 source ↗
  • For the following steps, prepare:
  • Door panel assembly (1x) you removed earlier
  • M3x5rT screw (4x) you removed earlier
  • Top door seal (1x) found in the Top Door Seal bag

Mounting the door panel

INDX 5.99 source ↗
  • Peel away the bottom backing layer of the gasket to expose the adhesive surface.
  • Align the gasket on the front profile with the adhesive side facing the surface, then press it down to adhere.
  • ReminderIf you had any issues with the shaft falling out of the hinge, assemble the hinge now, before mounting the door panel.
  • Insert the door panel fully into the hinges.
  • CautionEnsure the door panel is oriented correctly, with the handle facing outward. Use the V-shaped cutouts on the inner side of the door handle as a guide.
  • Insert two M3x5rT screws into each Door-hinge to secure the door panel.
  • Secure the screws gently to avoid over-tightening or damaging the door panel.

Attaching the stickers: Parts preparation

INDX 5.100 source ↗
  • For the following step, prepare:
  • CORE One+ sticker (1x) found in the INDX Update Stickers bag
  • INDX SN label (1x) found in the INDX Update Stickers bag
  • NoteIf you are installing the GEN 2 upgrade for the CORE One+ along with the INDX conversion, note that the "+" sticker is orange, not white.

Attaching the upgrade sticker

INDX 5.101 source ↗
  • Remove the sticker from the blue base.
  • On the door panel, align the sticker with the ONE and gently but firmly apply pressure to the sticker.
  • Carefully peel off the transparent layer and make sure that + is not peeling off.

Attaching the SN sticker

INDX 5.102 source ↗
  • Peel the Prusa INDX SN sticker off the base.
  • Place it on the back of the printer above the current CORE One/+ SN sticker.

Haribo time !

INDX 5.103 source ↗
  • You’re almost there. Take a break and get ready for the final chapter.
  • Eat eight gummy bears.
  • NoteNow you have only one gummy bear left. Maybe more, depending on the factory filling. But we have one more reward coming, so keep the rest aside!

That's it

INDX 5.104 source ↗
  • Congratulations! You have successfully upgraded your printer to the Prusa INDX edition!
  • NoteNext, you only need to run the self-test and basic calibration.
  • Proceed to the next chapter.

INDX 6. Preflight check steps all of 26 · Easy

Installing the spoolholder: Parts preparation

INDX 6.1 source ↗
  • NoteListed are the parts needed for the 8-tool version of the printer. For the 4-tool version, you will need half of the parts.
  • For the next step, prepare:
  • Telescopic spoolholder (8x) found in the Telescopic Spoolholder Set bag
  • O-ring (8x) found in the Telescopic Spoolholder Set bag

Locking the spoolholders

INDX 6.2 source ↗
  • Put the O-ring onto the telescopic spoolholder.
  • Ensure that the O-ring is placed correctly.
  • Push the telescopic spoolholder into the Puck-universal dock.
  • Lock the telescopic spoolholder by turning it clockwise.
  • ReminderRepeat the same procedure for the remaining spoolholders.

Telescopic spoolholders

INDX 6.3 source ↗
  • To extend the telescopic spoolholder, gently turn it counter-clockwise until you hear the locking mechanism snap.
  • Do not use excessive force to unlock the spoolholder, or you risk disengaging it from the puck holder!
  • Pull the spoolholder to extend it.
  • Lock the extended spoolholder by turning it clockwise until the lock snaps in place.

Attaching the print sheet

INDX 6.4 source ↗
  • CautionMake sure there is nothing on the heatbed. The heatbed must be clean. Any dirt can damage the surface of both the heatbed and the print sheet.
  • Attach the sheet by first aligning the rear cutout with the locking pins on the back of the heated bed. Hold the sheet by the front two corners and slowly lay it down onto the heated bed - watch your fingers!
  • Keep the print sheet clean for optimum performance.
  • #1 cause of prints detaching from the print surface is a greasy print sheet. Use IPA (Isopropyl alcohol) to degrease it if you have touched its surface before.

Firmware update

INDX 6.5 source ↗
  • Visit the help.prusa3d.com page.
  • Navigate to the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX page.
  • Download the latest firmware version.
  • Save the firmware file (.bbf) onto a USB drive.

Turning on the printer

INDX 6.6 source ↗
  • Insert the USB drive into your printer.
  • Connect the power cable and plug the printer into a wall outlet.
  • Turn the printer on using the switch on the back.
  • NoteThe printer will now detect if a new firmware file is available on the USB drive.
  • If the "New firmware available" screen appears, hit FLASH by pressing the rotary knob to upgrade to the latest firmware.

Setting up the printer: Intro

INDX 6.7 source ↗
  • The printer displays on the screen a prompt to select your language. Use the control knob or touchscreen to set your preference.
  • After selecting your language, the printer will display the welcome screen. Hit OK to continue through the setup process.
  • The next screen will prompt you to select your printer model COREONEINDX. Hit Done to continue.

Setting up the printer: Network setup

INDX 6.8 source ↗
  • The Network Setup screen will ask you to connect to a Wi-Fi network using our official Prusa mobile app.
  • NoteRead more on prusa.io/app.
  • If you select No, the printer will show alternative ways to connect to Wi-Fi. This step is optional and can be done later.
  • NoteYou can skip this screen and set up the network connection later.

Wizard: Intro

INDX 6.9 source ↗
  • NoteThe printer will prompt you to run self-tests and calibrations for all important components. The entire process takes a few minutes, with some parts requiring direct user interaction.
  • Hit YES to begin the self-test and follow the instructions on screen.
  • CautionDuring the self-test, keep the door closed until you are prompted. Opening the door will interrupt the process.
  • There are HOT and moving parts inside during the self-test.
  • NoteSome of the automatic tests that do not require direct input from the user are not mentioned in this guide.

Wizard: Door sensor calibration

INDX 6.10 source ↗
  • NoteThis step can be skipped. The door sensor is only calibrated during assembly and has a dedicated calibration section at the end of its own guide.
  • Hit the Skip button to proceed to the next calibration.
  • Follow the instructions on the screen. The printer will now run the automatic X-axis and Y-axis test, and the Z alignment calibration.

Wizard: Belt tensioning

INDX 6.11 source ↗
  • The printer will now prompt you to fine-tune the belts. Follow the on-screen instructions.
  • Open the top lid and manually move the INDX Tool head as far back as possible and check that there are no gaps between the stops on the left and right.
  • CautionWARNING: Incorrect procedure may result in damage to plastic parts or seizing of screws. Before adjusting the belt tension, read the dedicated article:
  • Adjusting belt tension (CORE One)
  • The belts are adjusted using the tensioning mechanism on each side for each belt:
  • The left screw adjusts the upper belt.
  • The right screw adjusts the lower belt.
  • Once the belts are perfectly tuned, press Continue and follow the on-screen instructions.

Wizard: Dock calibration I.

INDX 6.12 source ↗
  • Once the automatic homing calibration is complete, calibrate the docks. Hit Continue and follow the on-screen instructions.
  • The printer will ask you to enter the number of docks on your printer.
  • It means how many tool dock positions are installed on the front profile (nozzle holders). This is typically 4 or 8.
  • On the next screen, ensure that all dock positions are set to <Calibrate> and not to <Skip>.
  • Once all docks are ready to be calibrated, scroll down and hit Continue.

Wizard: Dock calibration II.

INDX 6.13 source ↗
  • The screen will now prompt you to tighten the silver screws securing each dock to the front profile.
  • Use a T10 key/screwdriver to tighten the silver screws in all positions.
  • Do not overtighten them, as they will be loosened again later.
  • Hit Continue.
  • NoteMake sure to follow the on-screen guide in the next step. The printer will inform you when it is safe to touch it and calibrate the docks.

Wizard: Dock calibration III.

INDX 6.14 source ↗
  • ReminderKeep the top lid open.
  • You are now prompted to manually move the head onto the dock.
  • From above, carefully slide the INDX Tool head onto tool dock position 1 by hand.
  • Watch the alignment from above to ensure the head seats perfectly onto the hotend.
  • Once properly seated, you will feel a click indicating the correct position.
  • Hit Continue and repeat the same process for the remaining docks, following the on-screen instructions.
  • After all docks have been aligned, loosen the silver screws securing all dock positions by one full turn.

Wizard: Loadcell Test

INDX 6.15 source ↗
  • The next step of the wizard will prompt you to touch the nozzle to test and calibrate the Loadcell. During this procedure, the parts of the printer are not heated up, so you can touch them. Press Continue.
  • NoteLoadcell calibration requires the door to be open, as you must interact directly inside the printer.
  • Do not touch the nozzle yet, wait until prompted by the Tap nozzle NOW message.
  • Tap the nozzle from below. In case the Loadcell does not detect the touch, you will be prompted to repeat the step. Otherwise, you will see Loadcell test passed OK when it succeeds.
  • To allow the printer to continue with the Wizard, close the door.
  • ReminderAfter this test, the printer will run the automatic Z-axis test.

Wizard: Fan test

INDX 6.16 source ↗
  • The printer will test all the fans during this process. Be aware—it can get quite noisy for a while!

Wizard: Tool offsets calibration

INDX 6.17 source ↗
  • Select Continue, and the printer will proceed with testing the offsets for each toolhead.

Wizard: Nozzle cleaner calibration

INDX 6.18 source ↗
  • In the following steps, you will calibrate the nozzle with the wiper bin.
  • Once you press Continue, the Toolhead will move itself closer to the priming block on the nozzle cleaner.
  • In the tooldock, under position 8, there is an opening through which you can directly observe nozzle alignment on the silicone priming block.
  • NoteIf you look closely through the opening, you will see the V-shaped cutouts in the wiper base and the silicone priming block.
  • Manually move the head above the bin on the right side of the printer. Position it in the middle of the priming block as shown on the screen.
  • Through the opening, observe and align the head with the V-shaped cutout in the front priming block, as shown on the screen.

Wizard: Nozzle cleaner calibration Z/X-axis

INDX 6.19 source ↗
  • The printer will now prompt you to align the nozzle cleaner.
  • Manually adjust the head position so the nozzle is placed in the V-shaped cutout in the silicone priming block. Observe the alignment through the front opening in the tooldock.
  • The printer will lock the motors and warn you to remove your hands from the printer before proceeding with the calibration.
  • Use the universal wrench to precisely adjust the Wiper-adjuster until the nozzle fully fills the V-shaped cutout, touching both angled sides and the bottom. Check the alignment through the opening.
  • NoteThe Wiper-adjuster allows the bin position to be adjusted up or down.
  • Once the position is correctly set (see reference detail), select Continue and follow the on-screen instructions.

Wizard: Nozzle cleaner calibration Y-axis

INDX 6.20 source ↗
  • Now, the printer screen prompts you to align the nozzle on the Y-axis.
  • Manually move the INDX Tool head into the V-shaped cutout on the left side of the nozzle cleaner bin and precisely align it. The nozzle must not touch the walls.
  • The correct cutout is marked with "Y"
  • Observe through the open door.
  • The printer will lock the motors and warn you to remove your hands from the printer before proceeding with the calibration.
  • Once the alignment is perfect, press Continue and follow the on-screen instructions.

Wizard: Filament sensors calibration

INDX 6.21 source ↗
  • During each tool filament sensor calibration, you will need a short piece of filament. Prepare the filament and select Continue.
  • NoteThere should be no filament inside the extruder before the calibration process starts.
  • Place the filament spool on the spoolholder and, when prompted, guide the filament into the filament sensor at position 1.
  • Insert the filament only through the filament sensor; there is no need to feed it through the full length of the PTFE tube.
  • After calibration finishes press Continue to calibrate the next position.
  • ReminderOnce all the positions are calibrated, continue to the automatic calibrations of phase stepping and input shaper.

Wizard complete

INDX 6.22 source ↗
  • Congratulations! The Wizard is complete. Now let's test some prints.

Haribo time!

INDX 6.23 source ↗
  • All your hard work has paid off, and it’s time for the final reward. Finish all the gummy bears now.

Prusa knowledge base

INDX 6.24 source ↗
  • Go to the CORE One/+ INDX product page at prusa.io/coreone-indx and navigate to the Getting started section for additional information and resources.
  • You can also find more information at help.prusa3d.com:
  • ReminderFind software downloads, product manuals, and detailed assembly guides.
  • ReminderAccess troubleshooting tips and solutions for common questions.
  • ReminderTutorials and articles to help you get the most out of your printer.
  • NoteWe are adding new topics every day!

Give us feedback

INDX 6.25 source ↗
  • We know you’re eager to start printing, but we’d really appreciate it if you could take 3–4 minutes to share your thoughts on this manual: how clear it was, how easy it was to follow, and any ideas to improve it.
  • NoteThis feedback is a little different from the usual comments you might leave on individual steps.
  • Share your feedback here.
  • Thank you for helping us make our manuals even better!

Join Printables!

INDX 6.26 source ↗
  • Don't forget to join the biggest Prusa community! Download the latest models in STL or G-code tailored for your printer. Register at Printables.com
  • Looking for inspiration on new projects? Check our blog for weekly updates.
  • If you need help with the build, check out our forum with a great community :-)
  • NoteAll Prusa services share one user account.

Appendix: not on Prusa's route

Prusa's companion article never routes you into the Gen 2 preflight chapter; the INDX preflight (chapter 6 above) covers firmware, belt tensioning and the selftest. Listed here so you can check whether anything Gen 2-specific, in particular 'Changing the printer edition', still applies to an INDX printer.

Print Sheet

GEN 2 5.1 source ↗
  • Reinstall the print sheet.
  • CautionMake sure there is nothing on the heatbed. The heatbed must be clean. Any dirt can damage the surface of both the heatbed and the print sheet.
  • Attach the sheet by first aligning the rear cutout with the locking pins on the back of the heated bed. Hold the sheet by the front two corners and slowly lay it down onto the heated bed - watch your fingers!
  • Keep the print sheet clean for optimum performance.
  • #1 cause of prints detaching from the print surface is a greasy print sheet. Use IPA (Isopropyl alcohol) to degrease it if you have touched its surface before.

Attaching the stickers

GEN 2 5.2 source ↗
  • For this step, prepare:
  • CORE One+ sticker
  • GEN 2 SN sticker
  • Peel the CORE ONE+ sticker off the base and place it on the CORE ONE+ logo on the door.
  • Make sure to align the sticker with the outline of the "ONE".  Apply pressure and then remove.
  • Place the GEN 2 SN sticker above the original SN sticker on the back of the printer.

Belt tensioning

GEN 2 5.3 source ↗
  • NoteThis chapter will guide you through calibrating and preparing the printer for its first run. Starting with tensioning the belts:
  • The left screw adjusts the upper belt.
  • The right screw adjusts the lower belt.
  • CautionWARNING: Incorrect procedure may result in damage to plastic parts or seizing of screws. Before adjusting the belt tension, read the dedicated article:
  • Adjusting belt tension (CORE One)
  • ReminderDo not forget to come back here after adjusting the belts.

Firmware Download

GEN 2 5.4 source ↗
  • We will have to upgrade the firmware.
  • NoteThe CORE One+ requires firmware version 6.4.0 or newer.
  • Visit the CORE One+ support page on help.prusa3d.com.
  • Download the latest firmware file (.bbf).
    Save the file onto a USB drive.

Firmware Flash

GEN 2 5.5 source ↗
  • Insert the USB drive with the firmware file into the printer.
  • Connect the power cable.
  • Turn the printer on using the switch on the back.
  • Once the "New firmware available" screen appears, select the FLASH option.

Changing the printer edition

GEN 2 5.6 source ↗
  • ReminderAfter completing the CORE One+ (Gen 2) upgrade, change the printer edition to CORE One+ (Gen 2).
  • NoteThis is required because the Gen 2 uses belts and pulleys with a different tooth pitch.
  • Go to Settings → Hardware → Edition and select CORE One+ Gen2.
  • The printer will ask you to confirm the edition change. Select Yes.

Selftest

GEN 2 5.7 source ↗
  • After finishing the upgrade, we recommend visiting the menu Control -> Calibrations & Tests and run the Selftest from the start.

Finish

GEN 2 5.8 source ↗
  • ReminderCongratulations! Your upgraded CORE One+ (Gen 2) is ready to roll!
  • Happy printing!
